sections.title: SMM-M04-L01: Hooks, scripts and storytelling
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Write hooks that stop the scroll, structure short videos and carousels as small stories that keep people watching, and use copy-ready script formats for Reels, Shorts, carousels and long videos. **Time:** about 3 hours (50 minutes study, 2 hours 10 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### The first three seconds decide everything

People scroll fast. Instagram's advice to creators is to hook viewers in the first 3 seconds and watch the **View Rate** in Insights; YouTube's retention report shows an **Intro** figure for long videos: the share of viewers still watching after the first 30 seconds. Both are telling you the same thing: if the opening doesn't earn attention, nothing after it matters.

A strong hook works on three layers at once:

- **Visual:** movement, a face, a finished result, a surprising object, in the very first frame
- **Text on screen:** 3–7 words that make the promise, readable without sound
- **Spoken:** the first sentence, said directly and quickly, with no "Hi guys, welcome back"

### Ten hook types that work in any niche

| Hook type | Example |
| --- | --- |
| Result first | Show the finished biryani, then "Here's how ₹150 gets you this in Kuttiady" |
| Question | "Why is this tea shop full at 6 am every day?" |
| Number or list | "3 places to eat under ₹100 near the bus stand" |
| Mistake | "Stop doing this when you charge your phone" |
| Before and after | A dull shop counter, then the same counter rearranged |
| "Watch before you..." | "Watch this before you order a birthday cake" |
| Myth vs fact | "Pickles must be full of preservatives? Not these." |
| Local surprise | "This 60-year-old shop still makes soda in glass bottles" |
| Direct address | "Kuttiady people, this is for you" |
| Curiosity gap | "The owner told me why he never raises the price" |

Rules: the hook must be **true** and the video must **deliver it**. A hook that tricks people makes them leave early and feel cheated, and the system notices both.

### Keep the promise: retention

- **Get to the point.** Cut every pause, every "um" and every second that doesn't move the story.
- **Change something every few seconds:** a new shot, a zoom, a new caption line, a sound.
- **Pay off the hook** before the end, then stop. Don't add a long outro.
- **End well:** a clear call to action ("Save this for Saturday") or a loop that flows back to the start.

### Stories, not information

Facts are forgotten; stories are shared. Five structures you can reuse:

1. **Problem → struggle → solution** ("My phone died every afternoon... until the shop showed me this")
2. **Before → after → bridge** (show both, then how)
3. **Mistake → lesson**
4. **How it's made / behind the scenes**
5. **Person story:** a shop owner's 45-second story in their own words (with consent)

### Scripts save time

Even a 30-second Reel goes faster with a script: you shoot only what you need. Write it in the template below, read it aloud once, cut 20% of the words, then shoot.

### AI can help brainstorm

An AI assistant can suggest twenty hook ideas in a minute. Use it to get unstuck, then choose, check the facts and rewrite in your own voice. Module 13 covers the risks, such as generic, same-sounding hooks and made-up facts.

## Local example

Nisha's Oven wanted a Reel about her eggless chocolate cake. Her first draft started "Hi everyone, today I'm going to show you..." and people left in the first two seconds: in Insights, most viewers didn't make it past the start.

Her rewrite, scripted in 5 minutes:

| Time | Shot | On-screen text | Voiceover (Malayalam) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0–2 s | Knife cutting into a gooey slice | "Eggless. You won't believe it." | "ഇതിൽ മുട്ടയില്ല!" |
| 2–8 s | Mixing bowl, three ingredients | "The secret: curd + one trick" | "രഹസ്യം തൈരും ഒരു ചെറിയ സൂത്രവും" |
| 8–20 s | Batter in the tin, oven, timer | "40 min at low heat" | "ചെറിയ ചൂടിൽ 40 മിനിറ്റ്" |
| 20–27 s | Slice on a plate, a child's hand reaching (her own child, filmed by her) | "₹650 for 1 kg, order by 6 pm" | "നാളത്തേക്ക് ഓർഡർ ചെയ്യൂ" |
| 27–30 s | Back to the cut slice (loops to the start) | "Order on WhatsApp 👇" | — |

The new version kept more viewers past the first 3 seconds and brought 11 WhatsApp enquiries in a week, against 2 for the first one.

(Made-up example to show the method.)

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Instagram for Creators: What creators need to know about recommendations](https://creators.instagram.com/blog/instagram-recommendations-eligibility-tips-creators) | Re-read the "make engaging reels" tips: vertical video, 3-second hook, no watermarks | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Instagram for Creators: Helping creators of all sizes break through](https://creators.instagram.com/blog/helping-creators-of-all-sizes-break-through) | Re-read the tips on hooks and View Rate | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [YouTube Help: Measure key moments for audience retention](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/9314415) | Read about the Intro, top moments, spikes and dips in retention | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [YouTube Creators: Shorts (how to record, add sound, edit and upload)](https://www.youtube.com/creators/create/shorts/) | Read the steps for recording, adding sound and editing a Short | 15 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [HubSpot Academy: Social Media Certification Course (free)](https://academy.hubspot.com/courses/social-media) | Watch the lesson on social content strategy (lesson names may change) | 15 min | verified 2026-10-25 |

## Action task

1. Study the resources (about 50 minutes).
2. Write 10 hooks for your pillars, using at least 5 different hook types. Add them to the Hooks and Captions tab.
3. Write 3 short-video scripts (30–60 seconds) with the template, each with a different story structure.
4. Write 1 carousel script (6–10 slides) with the carousel template.
5. Record and post the strongest script this week. Log it, and after 7 days compare its views and watch time with your earlier videos.

**Proof to record:** Your 10 hooks, 3 video scripts and 1 carousel script, and the link to the posted video with its Posting Log row.

## Template: short video script (Reel or Short, 30-60 seconds)

```
TITLE: ____________  PILLAR: ________  LENGTH: ___ s
HOOK (0-3 s)
  Visual: ______________________________
  On-screen text (3-7 words): ___________
  First sentence: ______________________
SET-UP (3-10 s): why this matters ______
VALUE (10-45 s): 2-4 beats, one shot each
  1. ____________  2. ____________
  3. ____________  4. ____________
PAYOFF (last 5-10 s): ___________________
CALL TO ACTION: save / share / follow / WhatsApp
SHOT LIST: ____________________________
MUSIC: none / platform library / Audio Library
CONSENT NEEDED FROM: __________________
```

## Template: carousel script (6-10 slides)

```
Slide 1 (cover): hook + promise, max 8 words
Slide 2: the problem or why it matters
Slides 3-8: one idea per slide, a short headline
            and 1-2 lines of text each
Slide 9: summary or "the one thing to remember"
Slide 10: call to action (save, share, DM, visit)
Caption first line repeats the hook in words.
```

## Template: long video outline (YouTube)

```
0:00-0:30  Hook and promise (what they'll get)
0:30-1:00  Why trust you / what you checked
CHAPTER 1: ____________ (00:00 must be listed first)
CHAPTER 2: ____________
CHAPTER 3: ____________
PAYOFF: the answer or result, clearly
END (last 20 s): one call to action, one next video
```

## Common mistakes

- **Starting with a greeting or your logo.** Start with the most interesting moment. Introduce yourself later, or not at all.
- **Clickbait.** A hook the video doesn't deliver makes people leave and stop trusting you.
- **Explaining everything.** One idea per short video. Save the rest for the next post.
- **Scripts that sound written.** Read them aloud; cut long sentences; say it the way you'd tell a friend.
- **No call to action.** Tell people the one thing to do next.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. Which opening is the strongest hook?
    - A) A long caption
    - B) "Hi everyone, welcome back to my page"
    - C) Your logo for 3 seconds
    - D) The finished result in the first frame with "₹150 gets you this in Kuttiady"
2. What does YouTube's "Intro" retention figure show?
    - A) Your upload schedule
    - B) Your subscriber count
    - C) The number of likes
    - D) The share of viewers still watching after the first 30 seconds
3. Why must a hook be true?
    - A) It isn't important
    - B) If the video doesn't deliver, people leave early and stop trusting you, and the system notices
    - C) True hooks are shorter
    - D) Platforms read every hook
4. A good way to end a short video is:
    - A) Repeating the intro
    - B) A clear call to action or a loop back to the start
    - C) A 20-second outro with music
    - D) Fading to black slowly

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** Instagram's and YouTube's guidance on hooks and retention, YouTube's Shorts guide and HubSpot's content lesson (about 50 minutes)
- **Action:** write 10 hooks, 3 video scripts and a carousel script, then post the best one. It is done when your proof is saved: your 10 hooks, 3 video scripts and 1 carousel script, and the link to the posted video with its Posting Log row.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **D.** It shows the result immediately and makes a clear, local promise.
2. **D.** It shows whether your opening matched what the title and thumbnail promised.
3. **B.** Satisfaction and watch time fall when a hook misleads.
4. **B.** Stop after the payoff and give one next step.

sections.title: SMM-M04-L02: Malayalam and English content
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Decide when to use Malayalam, English or both, type and design Malayalam text that renders correctly, add accurate subtitles, and test a post in two language versions. **Time:** about 1 hour 30 minutes (20 minutes study, 1 hour 10 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### Choose the language for the job

| Language | Strengths | Watch out for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Malayalam** | Trust, warmth and humour for local audiences; older viewers; strong emotion | Smaller reach outside Kerala; some search happens in English |
| **English** | Search, people from other states, professional audiences (LinkedIn), some Gulf followers | Can feel distant to local customers |
| **Both** | Malayalam speech or text plus an English caption line reaches both groups | Two languages crammed on screen become unreadable |
| **Manglish** (Malayalam in English letters) | Natural in comments and chats for many young people | Hard for some older readers; looks informal; inconsistent spelling hurts search |

Your research (SMM-M02-L02) is the guide: use the language your audience uses in its own posts and messages. Many local pages do well with **Malayalam speech, short Malayalam on-screen text, and an English first line in the caption** that carries the keywords people search for.

### Typing Malayalam on your phone

- **Gboard:** add Malayalam from Gboard's settings (Languages → Add keyboard), then hold the space bar to switch languages.
- **Indic Keyboard:** a free, open-source keyboard from the Malayalam computing community, with transliteration: type "kuttiady" in English letters and pick കുറ്റ്യാടി.

### Fonts that render Malayalam correctly

Malayalam has conjunct letters and chillu letters that some fonts break. Use fonts made for Malayalam, such as **Manjari** (Malayalam and Latin), **Chilanka** (handwriting style) or **Noto Sans Malayalam**, all on Google Fonts. Swathanthra Malayalam Computing, which created Manjari and Chilanka, notes that Google Fonts only includes fonts under free licences. Always check a finished design for broken letters before you post.

### Subtitles and captions

Many people watch without sound, so on-screen captions are essential.

- **In editing apps:** use auto-captions, then correct every word; automatic Malayalam captions often contain mistakes.
- **On YouTube:** set the video's language correctly. YouTube's automatic captions come from speech recognition and are made in the video's default language only, so for English subtitles on a Malayalam video, add a second track in YouTube Studio → Subtitles: upload a file, auto-sync a transcript, or type them yourself (as of October 2026).

### Translation without embarrassment

- Don't paste machine translations straight into posts. Ask a native speaker to check, and rewrite idioms rather than translating them word for word.
- Local words and Malabar expressions make posts feel real; never use a dialect or accent to mock anyone.
- Keep spellings consistent, especially place names, so people can search for them.

## Local example

**Amma's Pickles** tested the same Reel (a jar of mango pickle being filled) in two versions, one week apart:

| Version | Speech | On-screen text | Caption first line | Views (7 days) | WhatsApp enquiries |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | Malayalam | Malayalam only | Malayalam only | 2,100 | 9 |
| B | Malayalam | Malayalam, 4 words | "Malabar mango pickle, home-made in Perambra" | 3,400 | 14 |

Version B reached more people outside the immediate area, including Gulf-based Malayalis searching for "Malabar pickle", without losing local viewers. They kept B's pattern. One test isn't proof, so they planned to repeat it with two more products.

(Made-up numbers to show the method.)

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Gboard Help: Type in a different language](https://support.google.com/gboard/answer/7068494) | Follow the steps to add Malayalam and switch languages | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Indic Keyboard, free and open source (Google Play)](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=org.smc.inputmethod.indic) | Install it if you want transliteration from English letters | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Google Fonts: Manjari (Malayalam and Latin)](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Manjari) | Look at the Malayalam samples; download if you design on the laptop | 3 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Google Fonts: Chilanka (Malayalam handwriting style)](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Chilanka) | See the handwriting-style alternative | 2 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Swathanthra Malayalam Computing: Manjari, Gayathri and Chilanka in Google Fonts](https://blog.smc.org.in/manjari-gayathri-chilanka-in-google-fonts/) | Read the short post about these fonts in Google Fonts and Docs (in Malayalam) | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [YouTube Help: Add subtitles and captions](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/2734796) | Read the three ways to add subtitles on YouTube | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |

## Action task

1. Study the resources (about 25 minutes) and set up Malayalam typing on your phone.
2. Write your language rules: speech, on-screen text, caption first line, hashtags. Add them to your voice chart from SMM-M02-L04.
3. Make one post in two language versions (like the example) and plan to publish them a week apart at a similar time.
4. For a video with speech, correct the auto-captions word by word. On YouTube, add a second subtitle track in the other language.
5. Check every Malayalam design for broken letters at full size on your phone.

**Proof to record:** Your written language rules, links to both versions of the test post with their Posting Log rows, and a screenshot of corrected captions or a second subtitle track.

## Template: bilingual caption template

```
LINE 1 (English, with the search keywords):
  Malabar mango pickle, home-made in Perambra
LINES 2-3 (Malayalam, the story or the detail):
  അമ്മയുടെ കൈപ്പുണ്യം, ദിവസവും പുതിയ ബാച്ച്.
  250 ഗ്രാം ₹120.
CALL TO ACTION (both):
  Order on WhatsApp / വാട്സാപ്പിൽ ഓർഡർ ചെയ്യൂ: [number]
HASHTAGS (max 5): #malabarpickle #perambra
  #kozhikodefood #homemade #kudumbashree
```

## Template: language and subtitle checklist

```
[ ] Language chosen from audience research, not habit
[ ] On-screen text: one language, max 7 words a line
[ ] Malayalam font checked for broken letters
[ ] Place names spelled the same way every time
[ ] Auto-captions corrected word by word
[ ] YouTube video language set correctly
[ ] Second subtitle track added (if useful)
[ ] Translations checked by a native speaker
[ ] No dialect used to mock anyone
```

## Common mistakes

- **Two languages crammed on screen.** Pick one language for on-screen text; use the caption for the other.
- **Unchecked auto-captions.** Wrong captions look careless and can change the meaning. Fix every word.
- **Fonts that break Malayalam.** Use Manjari, Chilanka or Noto Sans Malayalam, and check at full size.
- **Inconsistent place-name spellings.** Choose one spelling (Kuttiady) and use it everywhere so search works.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. YouTube's automatic captions are made in:
    - A) Malayalam only
    - B) Every language
    - C) English only
    - D) The video's default language only
2. Which pattern often reaches both local and wider audiences?
    - A) Manglish on screen and in the caption
    - B) Malayalam speech and short Malayalam text, with an English first line in the caption
    - C) No text at all
    - D) English speech only
3. Why use fonts such as Manjari or Noto Sans Malayalam?
    - A) They make posts go viral
    - B) They are designed to render Malayalam letters correctly
    - C) They are the only legal fonts
    - D) Canva requires them

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** Malayalam typing, fonts and YouTube subtitles (about 25 minutes)
- **Action:** write your language rules and test one post in two language versions with corrected captions. It is done when your proof is saved: your written language rules, links to both versions of the test post with their Posting Log rows, and a screenshot of corrected captions or a second subtitle track.
- **Quiz:** at least 2 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **D.** For another language, add a subtitle track yourself.
2. **B.** The English line carries searchable keywords while the video stays local.
3. **B.** Some fonts break conjuncts and chillu letters.

sections.title: SMM-M04-L03: Shooting on your phone: light, sound and framing
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Shoot clear, well-lit, steady vertical video with clean sound on an ordinary Android phone, using free tools and things you already have at home. **Time:** about 4 hours (45 minutes study, 3 hours 15 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### Set up the phone before you shoot

- **Clean the lens** with a soft cloth. A smudged lens is the most common cause of hazy video.
- **Free up space** and charge the battery. Turn on Do Not Disturb so a call doesn't stop the recording.
- **Resolution:** 1080p at 30 frames per second is enough for social media and keeps files small on older phones. Use 4K only if your phone handles it smoothly.
- **Grid lines on** (in the camera settings) to help framing.
- **Lock focus and exposure:** tap and hold on your subject until the camera shows a lock, so brightness doesn't jump around.
- **Shape:** vertical 9:16 for Reels, Shorts and Stories; horizontal 16:9 for long YouTube videos. Decide before you press record.
- **Want manual control?** The free, open-source **Open Camera** app has manual controls, exposure lock and grids.

### Light: the cheapest upgrade

- **Face a window.** Soft daylight from the front or the side is the best free light. Put the window behind the phone, not behind the person.
- **Avoid harsh noon sun and bare tube lights overhead,** which make dark eye shadows. Outdoors, step into open shade.
- **Golden hour** (soon after sunrise and before sunset) gives warm, soft light for places and food.
- **Bounce light** with a white chart paper or a sheet of thermocol to brighten shadows; it costs a few rupees.
- **Keep it consistent** for a series, so your posts look like they belong together.

### Sound matters more than picture

Viewers forgive slightly soft video; they leave when they can't hear clearly.

- **Record in a quiet room** with soft things around (curtains, a bed, cupboards of clothes). Turn off fans and the TV.
- **Get the microphone close:** hold the phone at arm's length or closer when talking to camera.
- **Use what you have:** the wired earphones that came with many phones have a mic you can clip near your collar. A cheap clip-on microphone is an optional upgrade later.
- **Record voiceovers separately,** in the quietest corner, even under a blanket, then add them in the editor.
- **On the laptop,** Audacity is a free, open-source audio editor for recording and cleaning up voice.

### Framing

- **Eye level:** put the phone at the height of the person's eyes, not below the chin.
- **Rule of thirds:** place the eyes or the main object on a grid line, not dead centre.
- **Safe zones:** in vertical video the top and bottom are covered by the app's buttons and captions, so keep faces and text in the middle.
- **Clean background:** move clutter, switch off a flickering bulb, choose a plain wall.
- **Steady:** lean on a wall, rest the phone on a stack of books, hold with two hands and elbows tucked in. A phone stand is optional.
- **Hands-free:** the YouTube Shorts camera has a timer for hands-free recording.

### Shoot for the edit

For a 30-second Reel, shoot 8–12 short clips of 3–6 seconds each: a **wide** shot to show the place, **medium** shots of people or actions, and **close-ups** of details (hands, food, products). Shoot each action twice. These extra clips, called **B-roll**, make editing easy.

### Consent and safety while filming

- Ask before you film people, and ask shop owners before you film inside their shop. For children, ask a parent.
- Some places don't allow filming; respect the signs and the staff.
- Never film while driving or riding.

## Local example

Anu filmed a "Shop story" Reel at a tailoring shop in Kuttiady town. Her first attempt was in the shop's back room under a tube light, with the tailor's sewing machine running: dark eyes, harsh shadows and a voice you could hardly hear.

Second attempt, same day, with zero spend:

- She moved the stool near the front door so daylight fell on his face from the side.
- She asked for the machine to be switched off while he spoke, and recorded the machine sounds separately as background.
- She clipped her own wired earphones to his collar and recorded his voice on a second phone placed in his shirt pocket, as a backup.
- She shot 11 clips: wide shot of the shop, his hands on the machine, the measuring tape, his face as he laughed, the finished shirt.
- She asked his permission on camera and saved it in her consent note.

The Reel was a 40-second story of a tailor who has worked on the same street for 31 years. It became her most-shared post that month.

(Made-up example to show the method.)

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [YouTube Creators: Shorts (how to record, add sound, edit and upload)](https://www.youtube.com/creators/create/shorts/) | Read the recording steps: hold or tap to record, the timer and combining clips | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Open Camera, open-source camera app (Google Play)](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=net.sourceforge.opencamera) | Read the feature list; install it if your camera app has no manual controls | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Instagram for Creators: Best practices hub](https://creators.instagram.com/best-practices) | In "Creation", read the Reels pages | 15 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Audacity audio editor](https://www.audacityteam.org/) | Optional, on the laptop: read what Audacity does | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |

## Action task

1. Study the resources (about 35 minutes) and set up your camera: lens cleaned, 1080p 30 fps, grid on, Do Not Disturb.
2. Light test: record the same 10-second talking clip in three places (under a tube light, facing a window, in open shade outside). Compare them on your phone and note the best.
3. Sound test: record 10 seconds at arm's length with the phone mic, then with wired earphones clipped near your collar. Listen with earphones and note the difference.
4. Write a shot list for one Reel (8–12 clips: wide, medium, close-ups, plus B-roll).
5. Shoot it, with consent from anyone in it, and keep the clips for the editing lesson (SMM-M04-L04). If you can, edit it simply now and post it.

**Proof to record:** Your three light-test clips and two sound-test clips (or screenshots and notes), your shot list, and the folder of clips for your Reel.

## Template: shooting checklist

```
BEFORE
[ ] Lens cleaned  [ ] Battery 50%+  [ ] 2 GB free
[ ] Do Not Disturb on  [ ] 1080p 30 fps  [ ] Grid on
[ ] Shape decided: vertical 9:16 / horizontal 16:9
[ ] Consent asked (people, shop, parents of children)
LIGHT
[ ] Facing a window or in open shade
[ ] No bright window behind the subject
[ ] Focus and exposure locked (tap and hold)
SOUND
[ ] Fan, TV, machines off  [ ] Mic close
[ ] 5 seconds of silence recorded (room tone)
FRAMING
[ ] Eye level  [ ] Subject on a third
[ ] Faces and text away from top and bottom
[ ] Background tidy  [ ] Phone steady
SHOTS
[ ] Wide  [ ] Medium  [ ] Close-ups  [ ] B-roll
[ ] Each action twice
```

## Template: shot list

```csv
Shot,Type (wide/medium/close/B-roll),What happens,Length (s),Done?
1,Wide,Shop front with sign,4,
2,Medium,Owner at work,5,
3,Close,Hands on the product,4,
4,Close,Detail (price tag, texture),3,
5,Medium,Owner speaks: line 1,6,
6,B-roll,Customer or street (with consent),4,
```

## Template: consent note (save one per person)

```
Date: ____  Place: ____________
Name: ______________  Phone (optional): ________
I agree that [your page] may film me and post the
video on Instagram, YouTube and WhatsApp.
[ ] Yes, with my face  [ ] Voice only  [ ] Hands only
For a child: parent or guardian's name: _________
Can I ask to remove it later? Yes, message ______
(Record the yes on video or in a voice note too.)
```

## Common mistakes

- **A bright window behind the person.** Their face goes dark. Turn around so the window lights the face.
- **Recording next to a fan.** Fan noise ruins speech. Switch it off for the few minutes of recording.
- **Filming everything in one long take.** Shoot short clips from different angles; they are much easier to edit.
- **Text and faces at the very top or bottom.** App buttons cover them. Keep important things in the middle.
- **Filming people without asking.** Always ask, and save the consent. For children, ask a parent.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. Where should the window be when you film someone talking?
    - A) Above them
    - B) Behind them
    - C) It doesn't matter
    - D) In front of them or to the side, lighting their face
2. What usually makes viewers leave a talking video faster?
    - A) Vertical video
    - B) Slightly soft focus
    - C) A plain background
    - D) Unclear, noisy sound
3. Why shoot B-roll clips?
    - A) To have extra shots that make editing and pacing easy
    - B) Platforms require it
    - C) To make files bigger
    - D) To avoid captions
4. What does locking focus and exposure do?
    - A) Adds music
    - B) Makes the video private
    - C) Turns on 4K
    - D) Stops brightness and focus jumping around while you film

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** YouTube's Shorts recording guide, Open Camera and Instagram's Reels guidance (about 35 minutes)
- **Action:** run the light and sound tests, write a shot list and shoot the clips for a Reel. It is done when your proof is saved: your three light-test clips and two sound-test clips (or screenshots and notes), your shot list, and the folder of clips for your Reel.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **D.** Light on the face, not behind it, avoids a dark silhouette.
2. **D.** Sound problems are less forgiven than picture problems.
3. **A.** Close-ups and details let you cut quickly and keep attention.
4. **D.** Tap and hold on the subject to lock them.

sections.title: SMM-M04-L04: Editing on your phone
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Edit a short video entirely on your phone, from rough cut to captions, licensed sound and export, choosing a free editor that runs on your phone and leaves no watermark. **Time:** about 4 hours (45 minutes study, 3 hours 15 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### Choose an editor that runs on your phone (as of October 2026)

| App | Cost and watermark | Good for | Know this |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Edits** (by Instagram) | Free; exports with no watermark | Reels and Shorts: captions, green screen, cut-outs | Shows live insights for your reels |
| **YouTube Create** (by Google) | Free | Shorts and long videos: royalty-free music library, sound effects, auto-captions in some languages, voiceover | Needs Android 8.0 or later and at least 4 GB of RAM |
| **VN** | Free to download; has ads and in-app purchases | Multi-track timelines, auto-captions, teleprompter | Check the export screen for any paid features |
| **InShot** | Free to download; has ads and a Pro subscription | Quick trims, music, text, speed, resizing | Check export settings and watermarks before you rely on it |
| **Canva** | Free plan, no watermark on free elements | Video with text and templates | Paid Pro templates are marked |
| **Snapseed** (by Google) | Free, no ads or purchases | Photos: brightness, healing, perspective | Photos only |

On the old laptop, **Shotcut** and **Kdenlive** are free, open-source video editors. Kdenlive can make low-resolution proxy copies of your clips so that editing works even on a slow computer, and still export at full quality. **OBS Studio** records your screen for tutorials.

### The editing workflow

1. **Import** your clips and pick the best take of each.
2. **Rough cut:** put the clips in script order, hook first.
3. **Trim hard:** cut every pause, breath and "um". If a clip doesn't move the story, delete it.
4. **Captions:** generate auto-captions, then correct every word. Use large text with strong contrast, in the middle of the screen.
5. **Text overlays:** the hook in the first second; key numbers (prices, times) on screen.
6. **Sound:** voice first. Add music quietly underneath, from a licensed library (below).
7. **Colour:** small brightness and contrast fixes only; no heavy filters on food or faces.
8. **Cover:** choose a clear frame or upload a cover with the hook text in the centre.
9. **Export:** 1080 × 1920 (vertical) at 30 fps, then upload the file directly to each platform.

### Music and sound you're allowed to use

- **Add music inside the platform** when you post (Instagram's music library, YouTube's "Add sound"). Business accounts may have a smaller music library than creator accounts.
- **YouTube Audio Library** (in YouTube Studio) offers royalty-free music and sound effects. Tracks under a Creative Commons licence need the artist credited in your description; you can filter for "Attribution not required". YouTube says copyright-safe tracks downloaded from it won't be claimed through Content ID.
- **Never** download film songs or other creators' videos to use as background. "I gave credit" doesn't make it legal (Module 14).

### One video, every platform: export clean

Upload the original edited file to each app. Don't download your Reel from Instagram (with its watermark) and upload it to YouTube; platforms rank watermarked reposts lower.

## Local example

Riyas at **Malabar Mobiles** filmed a screen guard being fitted: 14 clips, 3 minutes 20 seconds of raw footage. In Edits on his phone, Anu helped him:

- **Cut** it to 25 seconds: the cracked old guard (hook: "₹199 saves a ₹4,000 screen"), cleaning, alignment, the bubble-free finish, the price on screen.
- **Captions** in Malayalam, corrected word by word, in white text with a dark outline.
- **Sound:** his voice for the first line, then the actual fitting sounds, plus a quiet track from Instagram's library when posting.
- **Export:** 1080 × 1920, no watermark; the same file uploaded to YouTube Shorts.

On Instagram, more viewers watched to the end than on his earlier, unedited clip, and on YouTube the Short kept getting views in search for "screen guard Kuttiady" weeks later.

(Made-up example to show the method.)

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Edits video editor by Instagram (Google Play)](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.instagram.basel) | Read the features; install it if your phone supports it | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [YouTube Create video editor (Google Play)](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.google.android.apps.youtube.producer) | Read the features and device requirements | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [VN photo and video editor (Google Play)](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.frontrow.vlog) | Read the features, ads and in-app purchase notes | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [InShot video editor (Google Play)](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.camerasideas.instashot) | Read the features and the ads note | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Canva Design School: Marketing with Canva](https://www.canva.com/en/design-school/courses/marketing-with-canva) | Watch "Social video editing basics" and "Advanced social video" | 15 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [YouTube Help: Use music and sound effects from the Audio Library](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/3376882) | Read how the Audio Library and attribution work | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Kdenlive video editor (features, including proxy clips)](https://kdenlive.org/en/features/) | Optional, on the laptop: read about proxy clips | 3 min | verified 2026-10-25 |

## Action task

1. Study the resources (about 45 minutes). Install one editor your phone can run smoothly.
2. Edit the clips from SMM-M04-L03 into a 20–40 second vertical video using the workflow: rough cut, hard trim, corrected captions, hook text, licensed sound, cover.
3. Edit a second video from new clips: a voiceover video (B-roll plus your recorded voice).
4. Export both at 1080 × 1920 and post them as Reels and Shorts from the original files.
5. After 7 days, compare their views and average watch time with your first videos from Module 1.

**Proof to record:** Links to both edited videos on Instagram and YouTube with their Posting Log rows, and a screenshot of the editing timeline or captions screen.

## Template: editing checklist

```
[ ] Best take of each clip chosen
[ ] Hook in the first second (visual + text)
[ ] Every pause, "um" and dead second cut
[ ] One idea; anything else saved for another post
[ ] Captions generated AND corrected word by word
[ ] Text large, high contrast, in the middle
[ ] Voice clear; music quiet underneath
[ ] Music from a platform library or the YouTube
    Audio Library (credit added if needed)
[ ] Light colour fixes only
[ ] Cover frame chosen, text centred
[ ] Exported 1080 x 1920, 30 fps, no watermark
[ ] Original file uploaded to each platform
```

## Template: export and upload card

```
REELS / SHORTS / STORIES: 1080 x 1920 (9:16), 30 fps
LONG YOUTUBE VIDEO: 1920 x 1080 (16:9), 30 fps
FILE NAMES: 2026-11-03_shopstory_tailor_v2.mp4
KEEP: the project file and the export, in Drive
      04 Content, until the post is 30 days old
UPLOAD: the original export to each app, not a
        download from another app
```

## Common mistakes

- **Unedited auto-captions.** Errors look careless. Correct every word before export.
- **Music louder than the voice.** Keep music low under speech. Voice first.
- **Heavy filters.** They make food and faces look fake. Small brightness fixes are enough.
- **Watermarked uploads.** Export your own file once and upload it to every platform.
- **An editor that crashes your phone.** Choose one that runs smoothly on your device, even if it has fewer features.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. What does YouTube Create need to run, according to its Play Store listing?
    - A) Any Android phone
    - B) A paid subscription
    - C) A laptop
    - D) Android 8.0 or later and at least 4 GB of RAM
2. Which music is safest for a 2-minute Short?
    - A) A royalty-free track from the YouTube Audio Library or YouTube's Shorts audio
    - B) Any song if you give credit
    - C) A film song downloaded from YouTube
    - D) A song from a friend's Reel
3. What does Kdenlive's proxy feature help with?
    - A) Adding ads
    - B) Removing watermarks from other videos
    - C) Translating captions
    - D) Editing on a slow computer using low-resolution copies, then exporting at full quality
4. The best way to post the same video on Instagram and YouTube is:
    - A) Post only on one
    - B) Download it from Instagram and upload to YouTube
    - C) Screen-record it
    - D) Upload your original export to each platform

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** The phone editors' listings, Canva's video lessons and YouTube's Audio Library guide (about 45 minutes)
- **Action:** edit two videos on your phone with corrected captions and licensed sound, and post them. It is done when your proof is saved: links to both edited videos on Instagram and YouTube with their Posting Log rows, and a screenshot of the editing timeline or captions screen.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **D.** Older or low-memory phones may need another editor.
2. **A.** Library tracks are licensed for use; credit alone doesn't give you rights.
3. **D.** Proxy clips make editing smooth on older laptops.
4. **D.** Watermarked reposts are ranked lower.

Action: edit two videos on your phone with corrected captions and licensed sound, and post them

sections.title: SMM-M04-L05: Design basics, carousels and thumbnails
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Use simple design principles to make readable carousels, Reel covers and YouTube thumbnails in Canva, within the free licence, with templates you can reuse. **Time:** about 2 hours 30 minutes (50 minutes study, 1 hour 40 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### Six principles for phone-sized design

Canva's free Design School teaches the elements and principles of design; for social media, six matter most:

1. **Contrast:** dark text on light, or light on dark. If you squint and can't read it, nobody will.
2. **Hierarchy:** one big headline, then smaller text. The eye should know where to start.
3. **Alignment:** line things up on one edge or centre. Random placement looks messy.
4. **Repetition:** the same fonts, colours and layout on every post builds recognition.
5. **Proximity:** keep related things together (a price next to its item).
6. **White space:** empty space makes the important thing stand out. Fewer words, bigger text.

Use your two brand colours plus white or black, and at most two fonts (one for Malayalam, such as Manjari, and one for English). Remember that most people see your design at the size of a matchbox.

### Carousels that get saved

- **Cover slide:** the hook and the promise, eight words at most, in the centre (the profile grid crops the edges).
- **One idea per slide:** a short headline and one or two lines.
- **Show, don't just tell:** photos, simple icons, numbers.
- **Summary slide:** the one thing to remember.
- **Last slide:** a call to action, such as "Save this" or "WhatsApp us to book".
- Instagram allows up to 20 items; most good carousels use 6–10.

### Thumbnails for YouTube

A thumbnail and a title are a promise; the video must keep it. YouTube's requirements (as of October 2026): a verified account; 16:9 for videos (9:16 for Shorts); JPG or PNG; at least 640 pixels wide; under 2 MB if you upload from the phone. In practice:

- **One clear subject:** a face showing emotion, or the product or place, big.
- **3–5 words** that add to the title rather than repeat it.
- **Strong contrast** and no clutter; check it at small size.
- **Consistent style** so viewers recognise your channel.

YouTube's **Test & compare** can try up to three titles or thumbnails and picks the winner by watch time, not clicks. It works on the computer only (SMM-M08-L03).

### Stay inside the free licence

Canva's free media licence lets you use its free photos, music and graphics in posts, ads and printed promotions, and you may edit them. You may not use them as part of a **trademark, logo or business name**, sell them as they are, or imply that people or brands in the images endorse your product. For logos, use your own text and shapes (ENT-M06-L01). Prefer your own photos anyway: real places beat stock images.

### Free tools beyond Canva

On the laptop: **GIMP** for photo editing, **Inkscape** for vector graphics such as logos and icons, and **Krita** for drawing and illustration, all free and open source.

## Local example

**Kakkayam Hills Homestay** made a 7-slide carousel, "Monsoon trip? Pack these 7 things", in Canva using its two colours (forest green and cream) and Manjari for the Malayalam lines:

1. Cover: a photo of misty hills from the homestay balcony, "Monsoon trip? Pack these 7" in big cream text
2–6. One item per slide with a photo they took (rain jacket, leech socks, torch, power bank, dry bag), one short line each
7. "Book a monsoon stay: WhatsApp 9XXXXXXXXX", with the homestay's photo and a small map pin

It was saved 140 times and shared 60 times in a week, far more than their usual room photos, and three people mentioned it when they enquired. They turned the layout into a template and reused it for "5 dishes we serve at breakfast".

For their YouTube room tour they made a thumbnail: the balcony view, the words "₹2,500 a night, this view", and a small face of the owner smiling.

(Made-up example to show the method.)

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Canva Design School: Graphic design essentials](https://www.canva.com/design-school/courses/graphic-design-essentials/) | Do the first 5 lessons: elements and principles of design | 25 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Canva Free Media License](https://www.canva.com/policies/free-media) | Read what you can and can't do with free media, especially logos | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [YouTube Help: Add custom thumbnails](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/72431) | Re-read the thumbnail requirements | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [GIMP image editor](https://www.gimp.org/) | Optional, on the laptop: look at what GIMP can do | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Inkscape vector graphics editor](https://inkscape.org/about/) | Optional, on the laptop: look at what Inkscape can do | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |

## Action task

1. Study the resources (about 45 minutes).
2. Make a carousel template in Canva with your colours and fonts: cover, content slide, summary slide and CTA slide.
3. Use it to make one 6–10 slide carousel from your carousel script (SMM-M04-L01) and post it.
4. Make one YouTube thumbnail for your planned long video, and one Reel cover, using the checklist.
5. Check every design on your phone at small size, and once in Malayalam for broken letters.

**Proof to record:** Your carousel post link with its Posting Log row, your reusable template, and your thumbnail and Reel cover images.

## Template: design checklist

```
[ ] Readable at matchbox size (squint test)
[ ] One headline, clearly the biggest thing
[ ] Max 2 fonts (Malayalam + English), 2 brand colours
[ ] Text aligned; nothing floating randomly
[ ] White space around the key message
[ ] Key text in the centre (grid and app overlays)
[ ] Malayalam checked for broken letters
[ ] Own photos, or Canva free media used within the
    licence (never in a logo or business name)
[ ] Same layout as my last posts (repetition)
```

## Template: carousel and thumbnail specs

```
CAROUSEL SLIDE: 1080 x 1350 (portrait) or 1080 x 1080
  Slide 1 hook | slides 2-8 one idea each |
  summary | call to action
REEL COVER: 1080 x 1920, text in the middle third
YOUTUBE THUMBNAIL: 16:9, e.g. 1280 x 720, JPG or PNG,
  under 2 MB from the phone, 3-5 words, one subject
```

## Common mistakes

- **Too much text.** If a slide needs a paragraph, it's two slides, or a caption.
- **Five fonts and seven colours.** Two fonts and two colours look professional and recognisable.
- **Thumbnails that lie.** Viewers leave quickly when the video doesn't match, which hurts it in recommendations.
- **Canva library elements in a logo.** The free licence forbids it. Build logos from your own text and shapes.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. What does Canva's free media licence forbid?
    - A) Editing the photos
    - B) Using free photos in social posts
    - C) Using free media as part of a logo, trademark or business name
    - D) Printing posters
2. How does YouTube's Test & compare choose a winning thumbnail?
    - A) At random
    - B) By watch time
    - C) By clicks
    - D) By likes
3. Where should key text go on a carousel cover?
    - A) Only in the caption
    - B) In the centre, because the grid crops the edges
    - C) Upside down
    - D) At the very edges
4. Which principle is "the same fonts, colours and layout every time"?
    - A) White space
    - B) Proximity
    - C) Contrast
    - D) Repetition

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** Canva's design essentials, its free media licence and YouTube's thumbnail rules (about 45 minutes)
- **Action:** make a carousel template, post a carousel, and design a thumbnail and a Reel cover. It is done when your proof is saved: your carousel post link with its Posting Log row, your reusable template, and your thumbnail and Reel cover images.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **C.** Others can use the same media, so you can't own it as your mark.
2. **B.** YouTube optimises the test for watch time.
3. **B.** The profile grid shows a cropped rectangle of the cover.
4. **D.** Repetition builds recognition.

sections.title: Module 5: Copywriting
sections.summary: Write words that make people stop, read, believe and act: headlines, captions, calls to action and platform-specific copy, persuasive without hype.
sections.content:
## Overview

Good copy is clear, specific and honest. In two weeks you'll learn headline and caption formulas, write calls to action for every stage of the funnel, practise honest persuasion inside Indian advertising rules, and adapt one idea to every platform you use.

The module ends with a caption bank for your 30-day challenge, so that when the challenge starts in week 14 you're never stuck for words.

## Outcomes

By the end of this module you can:

- Write first lines that work as headlines and carry keywords
- Use six caption formulas in English and Malayalam
- Write specific calls to action for each funnel stage
- Persuade honestly, avoiding hype, false urgency and engagement bait
- Adapt one idea to Instagram, YouTube, WhatsApp, Facebook, LinkedIn, Threads and Google Business Profile

## Time

About 9 hours 30 minutes in total: 7 hours 30 minutes of lessons and 2 hours for the module project. Part-time: weeks 12–13.

## Lessons

1. SMM-M05-L01: Headlines, hooks and captions that get read (about 2 hours 30 minutes)
2. SMM-M05-L02: Calls to action and persuasion without hype (about 2 hours 30 minutes)
3. SMM-M05-L03: Writing for each platform: bios, posts, titles and messages (about 2 hours 30 minutes)

## Module project: A caption bank for your 30-day challenge

1. Plan the topics for the 30 days of your challenge (you'll finalise the calendar in SMM-M06-L01): at least 6 per pillar.
2. For each day, write a headline or on-screen hook and a caption using one of the six formulas. Use at least four different formulas across the 30.
3. Add one specific call to action to each, matched to the post's funnel job.
4. Check all 30 with the honest persuasion check and the caption check.
5. Keep them in the Hooks and Captions tab, marked by day.

**Proof to record:** The Hooks and Captions tab with 30 hooks and captions, each with a CTA, marked by challenge day.

## Self-assessment rubric

Score yourself honestly after the project. Move on when no row is a 1 and at least half the rows are 3. If a row is a 1, redo that part first.

| Criterion | 1: Not yet | 2: Getting there | 3: Ready |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Headlines | First lines are greetings or dates | Some strong first lines | Every first line works alone and carries a keyword |
| Caption craft | Walls of text | Readable, sometimes vague | Short lines, specific details, one idea, the right formula |
| Calls to action | None or several at once | Generic CTAs | One specific, easy CTA matched to the funnel stage |
| Honesty and rules | Hype and false urgency | Mostly honest | Every claim provable; no dark patterns or engagement bait |
| Platform fit | Same text everywhere | Some adaptation | Each platform gets the right format, length and tone |

## Short on time?

The minimum version, when PSC prep or work leaves little time:

- Rewrite 3 captions with formulas and post one.
- Write a CTA bank with one CTA per funnel stage.
- Adapt one idea to two platforms.
- Write 15 challenge hooks (captions can be written during the challenge).

## Revision flashcards

Cover the right-hand column, read the front, say the answer, then check. Repeat the ones you missed the next day.

| Front (say the answer aloud) | Back |
| --- | --- |
| Two jobs of a caption's first line? | Make the right person read on, and carry the search keyword. |
| What do AIDA and PAS stand for? | Attention, Interest, Desire, Action; Problem, Agitate, Solution. |
| Three qualities of a good CTA? | Specific, easy (one tap) and worth it for the person. |
| Google's rule for urgency in ads? | Make any urgency earned and valued. |
| Two dark patterns banned in India in 2023 that copywriters must avoid? | False urgency and disguised advertisements. |
| Maximum CCPA penalty for a misleading ad, first and repeat? | Up to ₹10 lakh; up to ₹50 lakh for repeats. |
| What is engagement bait? | Posts that ask for likes, comments, shares, tags or votes just to boost reach; Meta demotes it. |
| Where does YouTube look to match a search? | Title, description, tags and the video itself. |

## Top mistakes in this module

- **Writing for yourself, not the reader.** Every line should answer "why should they care?"
- **Hype to make up for weak content.** Fix the content; keep the words honest.
- **Never testing copy.** Change one thing at a time (the first line, the CTA) and compare results.

sections.title: SMM-M05-L01: Headlines, hooks and captions that get read
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Write first lines and headlines that make people read on, and captions that are easy to read on a phone, using six reusable caption formulas in Malayalam and English. **Time:** about 2 hours 30 minutes (40 minutes study, 1 hour 50 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### The first line is the headline

On most platforms people see only the start of your words before they decide: the first line of an Instagram or Facebook caption before "more", the title of a YouTube video, the opening of a LinkedIn post, the on-screen text of a Reel. Treat that line as a headline. It has two jobs: **make the right person want to read on**, and **carry the keyword** they would search for.

Weak: "Today we visited a very nice place in our town and had a great time."
Strong: "Kuttiady's ₹60 meals with 9 curries (yes, really)"

### Headline formulas

Formulas aren't cheating; they are patterns that have worked for decades. Fill them with true, specific details:

| Formula | Example |
| --- | --- |
| How to [result] without [pain] | How to keep cream cakes fresh without a big fridge |
| [Number] [things] for [audience] | 5 phone habits that kill your battery |
| Stop [mistake] | Stop charging your phone overnight like this |
| Why [surprising fact] | Why this shop still sells soda in glass bottles |
| [Result] in [time] | A neat wardrobe in 15 minutes |
| [Place] people, [news] | Kuttiady people, the new bus timings are out |
| I tried [x] so you don't have to | I tried every chaya near the bus stand |
| The [specific] guide to [topic] | The honest monsoon packing list for Kakkayam |

### Make captions easy to read on a phone

- **Short lines** and blank lines between ideas. A wall of text gets skipped.
- **Simple words:** write like you speak to a neighbour.
- **Specific details:** prices (₹650), times (6 pm), places (near the bus stand), numbers. Specific feels true; vague feels like an ad.
- **One idea per caption.** If you have three ideas, you have three posts.
- **Emojis as signposts,** not decoration: one at the start of a list item is enough.
- **Keywords in the text**, written naturally, so search can find you. At most five specific hashtags at the end.

### Six caption formulas

1. **Hook – story – CTA:** the first line hooks, three to five lines tell the story, one line asks for action.
2. **Hook – 3 points – CTA:** best for tips and carousels.
3. **AIDA:** Attention (hook), Interest (a surprising detail), Desire (what they get), Action (what to do).
4. **PAS:** Problem, Agitate (why it matters), Solution. Keep the agitation gentle and true; don't scare people.
5. **BAB:** Before, After, Bridge (how to get from one to the other).
6. **FAQ caption:** the three questions people always ask, answered in one post.

### Length: match the format

- **Reels and Shorts:** the video does the work; one to three lines plus the CTA.
- **Carousels and photo stories:** longer captions are fine if every line earns its place.
- **LinkedIn and Threads:** the text is the post; hook in the first line, short paragraphs.

### Proof in every caption

Add one piece of proof whenever you can: a number, a real customer quote (with permission), a fact you checked, years of experience. Proof turns a claim into something people believe.

## Local example

Peak Fitness's original caption under a Reel of a trainer correcting a squat:

"Come and join Peak Fitness!!! Best gym in Vatakara with all facilities. Contact now. #gym #fitness #workout #motivation #viral #explore #reels #fit #health #instagood"

Rewritten with Hook – 3 points – CTA:

"Your knees hurt after squats? It's probably this. 👇

1️⃣ Knees caving in: push them out over your toes
2️⃣ Heels lifting: sit back, weight on your heels
3️⃣ Going too low too soon: start with a box behind you

Beginners' batch, 6–8 am, first session free. WhatsApp 'SQUAT' to 9XXXXXXXXX.

#vatakara #vatakaragym #kozhikodefitness #beginnerworkout"

Same video. The new caption was saved four times as often, and nine people sent "SQUAT" on WhatsApp in the first week.

(Made-up example to show the method.)

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Google Ads Help: Write compelling, genuine ad copy](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/6167101) | Read Google's advice on genuine copy: user benefits, specific calls to action, earned urgency | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [HubSpot Academy: Social Media Certification Course (free)](https://academy.hubspot.com/courses/social-media) | Watch the lesson on social content (lesson names may change) | 20 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Instagram for Creators: What creators need to know about recommendations](https://creators.instagram.com/blog/instagram-recommendations-eligibility-tips-creators) | Re-read the tip on keywords and hashtags in captions | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |

## Action task

1. Study the resources (about 35 minutes).
2. Take your 5 most recent captions. Rewrite each first line with a headline formula, and each body with one of the six caption formulas.
3. Write 10 new headlines from the formula table for your coming posts.
4. Publish two posts this week with the new captions, and log them.
5. After 7 days, compare saves, shares and replies with your older posts.

**Proof to record:** Your 5 before-and-after captions, 10 new headlines and links to the 2 published posts with their Posting Log rows.

## Template: caption formulas

```
HOOK - STORY - CTA
  Line 1: [hook with keyword]
  Lines 2-5: [what happened, specific details]
  Last line: [one action]

HOOK - 3 POINTS - CTA
  Line 1: [problem or promise]
  1. ______  2. ______  3. ______
  Last line: [save / share / WhatsApp keyword]

AIDA: Attention ____ / Interest ____ /
      Desire ____ / Action ____
PAS:  Problem ____ / Agitate (true, gentle) ____ /
      Solution ____
BAB:  Before ____ / After ____ / Bridge ____
FAQ:  Q1 ____ A1 ____ / Q2 ____ A2 ____ /
      Q3 ____ A3 ____ / CTA ____
```

## Template: caption check before posting

```
[ ] First line works alone as a headline
[ ] The keyword someone would search is in the text
[ ] Short lines, blank lines between ideas
[ ] At least one specific detail (Rs, time, place, number)
[ ] One idea only
[ ] One clear call to action
[ ] Max 5 specific hashtags
[ ] Read aloud once: sounds like me (voice chart)
```

## Common mistakes

- **Starting with "Hello friends" or the date.** Start with the most interesting line.
- **Walls of text.** Break it into short lines; delete anything that doesn't add.
- **"Best in Kerala!!!"** Unprovable superlatives sound like ads and can mislead. Use specific, true details.
- **Ten generic hashtags.** Five specific ones; and remember Instagram now allows only five.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. Which first line is strongest?
    - A) "Today we visited a nice place"
    - B) "Please like and share"
    - C) "Kuttiady's ₹60 meals with 9 curries (yes, really)"
    - D) "Hello friends"
2. What does PAS stand for?
    - A) Post, Add, Share
    - B) Photo, Audio, Story
    - C) Problem, Agitate, Solution
    - D) Price, Ask, Sell
3. Why include specific details such as ₹650 or 6 pm?
    - A) They make posts longer
    - B) Specific details feel true and answer questions before people ask
    - C) They replace the call to action
    - D) Platforms require numbers

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** Google's guide to genuine copy, HubSpot's content lesson and Instagram's caption tips (about 35 minutes)
- **Action:** rewrite 5 captions, write 10 headlines and publish 2 posts with the new captions. It is done when your proof is saved: your 5 before-and-after captions, 10 new headlines and links to the 2 published posts with their Posting Log rows.
- **Quiz:** at least 2 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **C.** It is specific, local and makes you want to read on.
2. **C.** Keep the agitation gentle and true.
3. **B.** Specificity builds belief and saves a message.

sections.title: SMM-M05-L02: Calls to action and persuasion without hype
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Write clear calls to action for each funnel stage, and persuade with honest proof, real reasons and true urgency, staying within Indian advertising rules. **Time:** about 2 hours 30 minutes (40 minutes study, 1 hour 50 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### A call to action is one clear next step

Every post should end with exactly one thing to do, matched to its job in the funnel (SMM-M01-L02):

| Funnel job | Good calls to action |
| --- | --- |
| Awareness | "Send this to someone who loves biryani", "Follow for one food spot every Friday" |
| Consideration | "Save this for your next trip", "Comment your question, we'll answer in the next post" |
| Conversion | "WhatsApp 'CAKE' to 9XXXXXXXXX", "Book on the link in bio", "Visit before 8 pm today" |
| Loyalty | "Join our WhatsApp Channel for weekly specials" |
| Advocacy | "Tag the friend who came with you", "Leave us a Google review: link in bio" |

Make it **specific** ("WhatsApp 'SQUAT'" beats "contact us"), **easy** (one tap: a WhatsApp link or button), and **worth it for them** ("get the price list", not "message us"). Google's own advice for ads makes the same point: generic calls to action such as "sign up today" or "call us today" don't tell people what they get.

### Honest persuasion

People decide with feelings and check with facts. These principles work and are fair:

- **Proof:** real reviews and messages shared with permission, photos of real work, numbers you can show.
- **Authority:** say why you know: "baking since 2014", "certified trainer", "we visited and paid for our own meal".
- **Usefulness first:** helpful posts earn the right to make an offer.
- **Clarity:** show the price, the size, the delivery area and the timing. Hiding the price feels like a trick.
- **Real urgency:** "Onam orders close on Thursday because we bake by hand" is true and useful. Google's advice is to make any urgency "earned and valued".
- **Risk reversal you can honour:** "If the cake isn't right, we'll make it again", only if you will.

### What hype looks like, and why it's dangerous

- **Superlatives you can't prove:** "best", "No. 1", "100% guaranteed".
- **Fake urgency and scarcity:** "Only 2 left!" every day; countdown timers that restart. India's Central Consumer Protection Authority lists **false urgency** and **disguised advertisements** among the dark patterns it banned in 2023 (SMM-M14-L03).
- **Health, money and miracle claims:** "lose 10 kg in 10 days", "guaranteed returns". These can be misleading advertisements, and ASCI's guidelines expect health and finance advice to come from qualified people (SMM-M14-L01).
- **Fake reviews and testimonials.**
- **Before-and-after photos** that are edited or not typical.

Under the Consumer Protection Act, the CCPA can fine a manufacturer or an endorser up to ₹10 lakh for a false or misleading advertisement, and up to ₹50 lakh for repeat offences, and the 2022 guidelines expect endorsements to reflect a genuine, current opinion based on real experience (check current rules). That applies to you when you write ads or posts for clients.

### Engagement bait isn't a call to action

"Comment YES if you agree", "Like for part 2", "Tag 5 friends to win" ask for empty actions to trick the feed. Meta's content distribution guidelines include a policy on **engagement bait**, and Facebook has demoted such posts for years. Ask for actions that mean something: a real question, a save, a share with a reason.

## Local example

**Kakkayam Hills Homestay** wrote two versions of its monsoon offer.

Hype version: "🔥🔥 BEST homestay in Kerala!!! Only 1 room left!!! Book NOW before it's gone!!! 100% satisfaction guaranteed!!!" They had three empty rooms, so "only 1 room left" was false, and "best in Kerala" couldn't be proved.

Honest version: "Monsoon weekends, 3 rooms only. Mist from the balcony at 7 am, Kerala breakfast included, ₹2,500 a night for two. We have just 3 rooms, so weekends usually fill first: check dates on WhatsApp ('MONSOON' to 9XXXXXXXXX). Free cancellation until 3 days before."

The honest version got fewer likes but more WhatsApp chats, and none of the guests complained that the place didn't match the post.

(Made-up example to show the method.)

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Google Ads Help: Write compelling, genuine ad copy](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/6167101) | Re-read the parts on specific calls to action and earned urgency | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [PIB: Misleading advertisement guidelines and penalties (February 2023, PDF)](https://consumeraffairs.nic.in/sites/default/files/PIB1897389.pdf) | Read what the misleading advertisement guidelines expect from endorsers, and the penalties | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25; check current rules |
| [PIB: Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023](https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1983994) | Read the press release on the 13 dark patterns | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25; check current rules |
| [Meta Transparency Center: Engagement bait (content distribution guidelines)](https://transparency.meta.com/features/approach-to-ranking/content-distribution-guidelines/engagement-bait/) | Open the page; read it in full in a browser if you can | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 (page title checked) |

## Action task

1. Study the resources (about 30 minutes).
2. Write a CTA bank: at least 3 calls to action for each of the five funnel stages, in English and Malayalam, and add them to the Hooks and Captions tab.
3. Take one offer (yours or a local business's) and write it twice: a hype version and an honest version. Mark every claim in the hype version that you couldn't prove.
4. Make a WhatsApp click-to-chat link for your page or a client (wa.me/ followed by 91 and the number) and put it in a post with a keyword CTA.
5. Publish two posts this week with specific, honest CTAs, and count the actions they bring.

**Proof to record:** Your CTA bank, your hype-versus-honest pair with the unprovable claims marked, and links to the 2 posts with the actions they brought.

## Template: CTA bank (English and Malayalam)

```
AWARENESS
  Send this to someone who ___ / ___ ഇഷ്ടമുള്ള ഒരാൾക്ക് അയക്കൂ
  Follow for ___ every ___ / എല്ലാ ___ നും ___ കാണാൻ ഫോളോ ചെയ്യൂ
CONSIDERATION
  Save this for later / പിന്നീട് നോക്കാൻ സേവ് ചെയ്യൂ
  Comment your question / സംശയം കമന്റ് ചെയ്യൂ
CONVERSION
  WhatsApp '___' to ___ / '___' എന്ന് വാട്സാപ്പ് ചെയ്യൂ
  Visit before ___ today / ഇന്ന് ___ ന് മുൻപ് വരൂ
LOYALTY
  Join our WhatsApp Channel / വാട്സാപ്പ് ചാനലിൽ ചേരൂ
ADVOCACY
  Tag the friend who came with you / കൂടെ വന്ന സുഹൃത്തിനെ ടാഗ് ചെയ്യൂ
  Leave a Google review (link in bio)
```

## Template: honest persuasion check

```
For every claim in the post:
[ ] Can I prove it today? (photo, review, number)
[ ] Is the price, size, area and timing clear?
[ ] Is any urgency true? (real deadline, real stock)
[ ] No "best / No. 1 / 100% / guaranteed" I can't prove
[ ] No health, weight-loss or money-return promises
[ ] Reviews and photos are real, used with permission
[ ] Before/after photos are unedited and typical
[ ] Paid or gifted? Disclosed clearly (Module 14)
[ ] No engagement bait (like/comment/tag for reach)
```

## Common mistakes

- **Several CTAs in one post.** Follow, like, share, DM and visit means people do none. Pick one.
- **"Contact us for details".** Give the details, then a specific action with a benefit.
- **Fake scarcity.** False urgency is a banned dark pattern and destroys trust.
- **Promising what the client can't deliver.** Check every claim with the business owner before posting.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. Which CTA is best for a conversion post?
    - A) "Follow for more"
    - B) "Contact us"
    - C) "Like and share"
    - D) "WhatsApp 'CAKE' to 9XXXXXXXXX for today's price list"
2. "Only 2 rooms left!" posted every day when rooms are empty is:
    - A) Required by Instagram
    - B) Good marketing
    - C) An honest CTA
    - D) False urgency, a dark pattern banned in India in 2023
3. What maximum penalty can the CCPA impose on an endorser for a false or misleading advertisement (first offence)?
    - A) ₹10,000
    - B) ₹10 lakh
    - C) ₹1 lakh
    - D) No penalty
4. "Comment YES if you agree!" written only to boost reach is:
    - A) Engagement bait, which Meta demotes
    - B) A strong CTA
    - C) A legal disclosure
    - D) Required for growth

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** Google's ad copy advice, the CCPA misleading-ads and dark-patterns releases and Meta's engagement bait page (about 30 minutes)
- **Action:** build a CTA bank, write a hype-versus-honest offer and post 2 honest CTAs. It is done when your proof is saved: your CTA bank, your hype-versus-honest pair with the unprovable claims marked, and links to the 2 posts with the actions they brought.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **D.** It is specific, easy and tells people what they get.
2. **D.** The CCPA's dark patterns guidelines list false urgency.
3. **B.** Up to ₹10 lakh, and up to ₹50 lakh for repeat offences (check current rules).
4. **A.** Ask for meaningful actions instead.

Action: build a CTA bank, write a hype-versus-honest offer and post 2 honest CTAs

sections.title: SMM-M05-L03: Writing for each platform: bios, posts, titles and messages
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Adapt one message to Instagram, YouTube, Facebook, LinkedIn, Threads, WhatsApp and Google Business Profile, using the format, length and tone each one rewards. **Time:** about 2 hours 30 minutes (30 minutes study, 2 hours action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### Same message, different shapes

People use each platform in a different mood, so the same idea needs different words. Here is how one idea, "Nisha's Oven now makes eggless cakes", changes:

| Platform | What to write | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Instagram Reel** | On-screen hook (3–7 words), a 1–3 line caption, keyword, max 5 hashtags | "Eggless. You won't believe it." / "Eggless chocolate cake, Kuttiady. ₹650 for 1 kg. WhatsApp 'CAKE' 👇" |
| **Instagram carousel** | Cover headline, one idea per slide, a longer caption that adds detail | "5 eggless cakes we bake every day" |
| **YouTube Short title** | The search phrase first, short enough to read in the feed | "Eggless chocolate cake, Malayalam recipe tip" |
| **YouTube long video** | Title with the search phrase; description's first 2 lines say what viewers get; chapters; links | "Eggless chocolate cake without an oven? (Malayalam)" |
| **Facebook Page or group** | Conversational, a little longer, a real question for comments | "Many of you asked for eggless cakes for your parents. Which flavour should we add next?" |
| **LinkedIn** | A professional lesson or result, short paragraphs, no hashtag walls | (For your own profile:) "What I learned helping a home bakery get 30 WhatsApp orders a month" |
| **Threads** | One thought or question that starts a conversation | "Eggless cakes: hit or miss? Honest opinions welcome." |
| **WhatsApp Status** | One photo or short video, one line | "Fresh eggless batch today 🎂 order by 6 pm" |
| **WhatsApp Channel or broadcast** | Personal, short, one CTA, how to stop | "Hi from Nisha's Oven! Eggless cakes are now daily. Reply STOP to stop these messages." (Channels can't receive replies, so give a number to WhatsApp instead.) |
| **Google Business Profile post** | An update, offer or event, with a button | "Eggless cakes now available daily. Order: call or WhatsApp." |

### YouTube titles and descriptions

YouTube's search looks at how well the **title, description, tags and the video itself** match a search (as of October 2026). So:

- Put the words people actually search near the start of the title, in the language they search in.
- Use the first two lines of the description to say what viewers get; YouTube shows only the start before "more".
- Add **chapters** for long videos: timestamps in the description, starting at 00:00, at least three, each at least 10 seconds long.
- Up to three hashtags from the description can show above the title; don't use unrelated hashtags.

### Messages and replies

Quick, warm replies turn interest into customers. Reply to comments within a few hours, answer the actual question, and move private details (phone numbers, addresses, payments) to WhatsApp or DMs. Save your best replies as templates.

### Bios are copy too

Each platform's bio should say who it's for, what they get and what to do, in the space that platform allows (SMM-M03-L01 has the formula).

## Local example

Anu turned one visit, a new juice shop in Kuttiady, into posts for four places:

- **Reel** (main): hook "₹40 fresh juice, no sugar added?" + 25 seconds of the shop + caption "New juice shop near Kuttiady bus stand: ₹40 seasonal juices, no sugar unless you ask. Open 10–9, closed Fridays. 📍 tagged."
- **YouTube Short:** the same video file; title "₹40 fresh juice in Kuttiady (no sugar)".
- **WhatsApp Channel:** "New spot: ₹40 juices near the bus stand, no sugar unless you ask. Video on Instagram: [link]."
- **Threads:** "What's your go-to juice in summer? Found a ₹40 place that doesn't add sugar."

Total extra time after the Reel: about 12 minutes. The Channel post brought 40 people to the Reel within an hour.

(Made-up example to show the method.)

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [YouTube Help: How YouTube search works](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/16090438) | Re-read the relevance section: titles, descriptions and tags | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [YouTube Help: Video chapters](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/9884579) | Read the rules for chapters | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [YouTube Help: Find playlists and videos using hashtags (hashtag rules)](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/6390658) | Read the rules for hashtags on YouTube | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [LinkedIn: LinkedIn Pages best practices](https://business.linkedin.com/advertise/linkedin-pages/best-practices) | Re-read the content tips (documents, images, hashtags) | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Business Profile Help: Get started with Google Business Profile](https://support.google.com/business/answer/7039811) | Read what you can add to a Business Profile | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |

## Action task

1. Study the resources (about 25 minutes).
2. Choose one strong idea from your Ideas tab and write it for five places using the table: a Reel caption, a YouTube title and description, a WhatsApp Channel or Status line, a Threads or Facebook post, and a LinkedIn post about what you learned making it.
3. Write 5 reply templates for common comments and DMs (price, location, timing, complaint, thank you).
4. Publish at least three of the versions this week and log them separately.

**Proof to record:** Your five platform versions of one idea, your 5 reply templates and the links to the published versions.

## Template: one idea, five places

```
IDEA: ______________________________
INSTAGRAM: on-screen hook ___________
           caption (1-3 lines + CTA + 5 tags) ____
YOUTUBE:   title (search phrase first) _________
           description line 1 ____ line 2 ____
           chapters (long videos) 00:00 ____
WHATSAPP:  Status line ____ / Channel post ____
FACEBOOK or THREADS: question or thought ____
LINKEDIN:  what I learned + one number ________
```

## Template: reply templates

```
PRICE:     Thanks for asking! It's ₹___ for ___. WhatsApp ___ to order.
LOCATION:  We're at ___ (pinned in the post). Open ___ to ___.
TIMING:    Yes, open on ___ from ___ to ___. See you!
COMPLAINT: Sorry about this. Please WhatsApp ___ so we can fix it today.
THANK YOU: Thank you so much! Can we share your message? 🙏
(Malayalam versions in the Hooks and Captions tab)
```

## Common mistakes

- **Copy-pasting the same caption everywhere.** Keep the idea, change the words for each platform's mood and format.
- **Keyword-stuffed YouTube titles.** One natural search phrase near the start, then a reason to click.
- **Arguing in public replies.** Acknowledge, then move the conversation to WhatsApp or DMs (SMM-M14-L04).
- **Broadcasts with no way to stop.** Always say how to opt out, and respect it.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. Where should the search phrase go in a YouTube title?
    - A) Only in tags
    - B) At the end, hidden
    - C) Near the start, in the words people actually search
    - D) Nowhere
2. What are the rules for YouTube chapters?
    - A) Any order, any length
    - B) Only for Shorts
    - C) Only paid channels
    - D) Start at 00:00, at least three timestamps, each chapter at least 10 seconds
3. Why should a WhatsApp Channel post give a number to message?
    - A) It looks longer
    - B) Numbers are required
    - C) Channel followers can't reply to updates
    - D) Channels are illegal

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** YouTube's search, chapters and hashtag rules, LinkedIn's content tips and Google Business Profile basics (about 25 minutes)
- **Action:** write one idea for five platforms, make 5 reply templates and publish at least three versions. It is done when your proof is saved: your five platform versions of one idea, your 5 reply templates and the links to the published versions.
- **Quiz:** at least 2 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **C.** Search compares titles, descriptions and the video with the query.
2. **D.** That is what YouTube Help requires.
3. **C.** Channels are one-way; give another way to reach you.

Action: write one idea for five platforms, make 5 reply templates and publish at least three versions
