sections.summary: **Outcome:** Read Instagram Insights, YouTube Studio analytics and WhatsApp Business statistics, work out the few ratios that matter, and turn your 30-day challenge numbers into clear decisions. **Time:** about 3 hours 30 minutes (45 minutes study, 2 hours 45 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### The numbers that matter, in plain words

| Metric | What it means | Why it matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Views** | How many times a post was seen, counting repeats | Instagram's main metric across formats since August 2024 |
| **Accounts reached** | How many different accounts saw it | Real audience size |
| **Non-follower share** | Views or reach from people who don't follow you | Your growth from recommendations |
| **Interactions** | Likes, comments, shares, saves | Signals of interest |
| **Shares and saves** | Sending to others, keeping for later | The strongest signs a post was valuable |
| **Watch time and retention** | How long people watch, and where they leave | Shows whether the hook and story worked |
| **Follows** | New followers from a post | Whether people want more from you |
| **Profile visits and link clicks** | People looking for more, or going to your link | Consideration |
| **Messages and enquiries** | DMs, WhatsApp chats, calls | Leads, the number businesses care about |

### Where to find them (as of October 2026)

- **Instagram:** open a post and tap **View insights**, or open the **professional dashboard** for the account. Look at Views, the split between followers and non-followers, interactions, and for Reels the watch time. Instagram's creator advice is to watch your **View Rate** in Insights to see whether your hook keeps people watching.
- **YouTube Studio** (phone app or computer): **Impressions** count when your thumbnail was shown for more than a second with at least half of it visible on YouTube. **Impressions click-through rate** shows how often an impression led to a view. **Average view duration** and the **audience retention** graph (intro, top moments, spikes and dips) show where people leave. **Traffic sources** show whether views came from search, the Shorts feed, browse or suggested videos. Data usually takes a day or two to appear.
- **Facebook:** Page insights in Meta Business Suite.
- **WhatsApp Business:** message statistics, and read and reply rates for business broadcasts.
- **LinkedIn:** analytics for your posts and Page.

### Ratios beat raw numbers

A post with 5,000 views and 2 shares did worse than one with 800 views and 40 shares, if your goal is to be shared. Calculate a few ratios per post:

- **Share rate** = shares ÷ views × 1,000 (shares per 1,000 views)
- **Save rate** = saves ÷ views × 1,000
- **Follow rate** = follows ÷ views × 1,000
- **Engagement rate** = interactions ÷ accounts reached × 100
- **Non-follower share** = views from non-followers ÷ views × 100

### From numbers to decisions

Look for **patterns** across many posts, not single surprises. Group your 30 challenge posts by pillar, format, hook type, length and language, and compare the averages. Then write each finding as **"So what? Now what?"**:

- "Shop stories have twice the share rate of food posts → so local people love people stories → post two shop stories a week."

### Be careful with small numbers

With 30 posts, differences of a few per cent can be chance. Treat findings as **directional** and test them again. And remember platforms change how they count: compare with your own past numbers, measured the same way.

## Local example

Anu put her 30 challenge posts in a sheet and grouped them (made-up numbers to show the method):

| Group | Posts | Average views | Shares per 1,000 | Follows per 1,000 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Shop stories | 6 | 3,100 | 19 | 9 |
| ₹100 food | 9 | 1,400 | 12 | 6 |
| Local updates (text-heavy) | 5 | 420 | 3 | 2 |
| Places and nostalgia | 6 | 1,050 | 15 | 4 |
| Collabs | 4 | 2,200 | 10 | 11 |
| Question hooks (all pillars) | 13 | 1,700 | 14 | 7 |
| Result-first hooks | 12 | 1,350 | 11 | 6 |

Her decisions: two shop stories a week; text-heavy updates move to the WhatsApp Channel; one collab a month, because collabs bring the most follows per view; keep testing question hooks, since the difference was small.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Social Samosa: Instagram makes Views its main metric (August 2024)](https://socialsamosa.com/news-2/instagram-updates-metrics-creators-prioritise-reach-6807009) | Re-read how Views became Instagram's main metric | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Instagram for Creators: Helping creators of all sizes break through](https://creators.instagram.com/blog/helping-creators-of-all-sizes-break-through) | Re-read the View Rate tip | 3 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [YouTube Help: Check your impressions and watch time](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/7577430) | Read what counts as an impression and how CTR works | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [YouTube Help: Measure key moments for audience retention](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/9314415) | Re-read the retention key moments and how to use them | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [WhatsApp Business: business broadcasts](https://whatsappbusiness.com/resources/resource-library/business-broadcasts-whatsapp/) | Re-read the broadcast metrics (read and reply rates) | 3 min | verified 2026-10-25; check current rules |
| [HubSpot Academy: Social Media Certification Course (free)](https://academy.hubspot.com/courses/social-media) | Watch the lesson on measuring social media results (lesson names may change) | 15 min | verified 2026-10-25 |

## Action task

1. Study the resources (about 45 minutes).
2. For all 30 challenge posts, make sure your Posting Log has 7-day views, reach, shares, saves, follows and (for videos) watch time or retention.
3. Add the five ratio columns and fill them with formulas.
4. Group the posts by pillar, format, hook type, length and language, and compare the averages.
5. Write 5 "So what? Now what?" findings with a decision each, and mark which ones need re-testing.

**Proof to record:** Your Posting Log with ratio columns, the grouped comparison table and your 5 findings with decisions.

## Template: ratio formulas for Google Sheets

```
(Assuming views in column J, shares in N, saves in O,
 follows in P, reach in K, interactions in Q, views from
 non-followers in R)
Share rate per 1,000:   =IFERROR(N2/J2*1000,0)
Save rate per 1,000:    =IFERROR(O2/J2*1000,0)
Follow rate per 1,000:  =IFERROR(P2/J2*1000,0)
Engagement rate %:      =IFERROR(Q2/K2*100,0)
Non-follower share %:   =IFERROR(R2/J2*100,0)
Group averages:         =AVERAGEIF(D:D,"Shop story",J:J)
```

## Template: findings: so what, now what

```
FINDING 1: ______________________ (numbers: ____)
  So what? _______________________
  Now what? ______________________
  Confidence: strong / directional (re-test)
FINDING 2: ...
(5 findings)
```

## Common mistakes

- **Reading only views.** Use ratios such as shares, saves and follows per 1,000 views.
- **Comparing with other people's accounts.** Compare with your own past numbers, measured the same way.
- **Deciding from one post.** Look at averages across groups of posts.
- **Checking too early.** Use 7-day numbers; recommended posts keep growing for days.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. Which post did better at being shared?
    - A) Impossible to say
    - B) They are equal
    - C) 800 views and 40 shares
    - D) 5,000 views and 2 shares
2. When does YouTube count a thumbnail impression?
    - A) Every time a video is uploaded
    - B) Only when clicked
    - C) When the thumbnail is shown for more than a second with at least half of it visible
    - D) When a video is shared
3. Your findings come from 30 posts and the difference is small. How should you treat it?
    - A) Delete the worse posts
    - B) As proof
    - C) Ignore all data
    - D) As directional, and test it again
4. Which number best shows growth from recommendations?
    - A) Posting time
    - B) The share of views from non-followers
    - C) Total likes
    - D) Number of hashtags

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** Instagram's and YouTube's metric definitions, WhatsApp broadcast stats and HubSpot's measurement lesson (about 45 minutes)
- **Action:** add ratios to your 30 challenge posts, compare groups and write 5 findings with decisions. It is done when your proof is saved: your Posting Log with ratio columns, the grouped comparison table and your 5 findings with decisions.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **C.** 50 shares per 1,000 views against 0.4 per 1,000.
2. **C.** That is YouTube's definition, on YouTube surfaces.
3. **D.** Small samples can mislead; re-test before big changes.
4. **B.** Non-follower views show the system is showing you to new people.

sections.title: SMM-M08-L02: Google Analytics 4 and UTM links
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Set up a free Google Analytics 4 property on a simple site, tag your social links with UTM parameters, and read which platform and post sent visitors. **Time:** about 3 hours 30 minutes (45 minutes study, 2 hours 45 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### Why bother with Google Analytics

Platform insights tell you what happened **on** the platform. When a post sends people to a website (a business's booking page, a menu, your portfolio), **Google Analytics 4 (GA4)** tells you what happened next: how many arrived, from which platform and campaign, and what they did. GA4 is free; Google's setup guide says it gives insights "at no cost".

### Set up GA4 in four steps (as of October 2026)

1. **Account:** sign in at analytics.google.com and create an account.
2. **Property:** name it ("Anu portfolio"), choose India's time zone and rupees.
3. **Web data stream:** add your site's address; turn on enhanced measurement.
4. **Add the tag:** copy the **Measurement ID** (it starts with "G-") into your site. On **Google Sites**, open Settings → Analytics and enter the ID. Google Sites' help notes that data can take up to 24 hours to show, and that visitors who reject cookies make the numbers lower than real.

Test it: open your site on your phone and check the **Realtime** report.

### A simple site to practise on

If you don't have a site yet, make a one-page **Google Sites** page now, such as "About @kuttiady.diaries" or a menu page for a friendly business. You'll turn it into your portfolio in Module 12.

### UTM links: labels on your links

A UTM link is a normal link with labels added at the end, so GA4 knows where each visitor came from. Google's rules:

- **Always use** `utm_source`, `utm_medium` and `utm_campaign`. Missing ones show up as "(not set)".
- **Optional:** `utm_content` (to tell apart two links in the same place), `utm_term` (paid keywords) and `utm_id`.
- **Values are case-sensitive:** `instagram` and `Instagram` are different, so always use lowercase.

Example:

`https://sites.google.com/view/yourpage?utm_source=instagram&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=bio_link`

Use Google's free **Campaign URL Builder** to make them without typing mistakes. Never put names, phone numbers or other personal details in a UTM.

### Read the results

In GA4, open **Reports → Acquisition → Traffic acquisition**. The **session source / medium** shows "instagram / social", "whatsapp / social" and so on; **session campaign** shows your campaign names; the default channel groups include **Organic Social** and **Paid Social**.

### WhatsApp is different

A WhatsApp click-to-chat link opens a chat, not a website, so GA4 can't see it. Track WhatsApp enquiries with **keywords** in your CTA ("send 'SQUAT'"), **labels** in WhatsApp Business and the question "how did you hear about us?".

## Local example

Peak Fitness made a one-page Google Site with its timetable and fees, connected GA4, and used three UTM links for two weeks:

| Where | utm_source | utm_medium | utm_campaign | Sessions (2 weeks) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Instagram bio | instagram | social | bio_link | 96 |
| WhatsApp Status | whatsapp | social | status_timetable | 41 |
| YouTube description | youtube | social | gym_tour | 18 |

Instagram sent the most visitors, but WhatsApp visitors stayed on the page longer and more of them messaged afterwards. The gym kept the bio link and started posting the timetable on Status every Monday.

(Made-up numbers to show the method.)

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Analytics Help: Set up Analytics for a website and/or app](https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/9304153) | Read the four setup steps | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Sites Help: Use Analytics with your site](https://support.google.com/sites/answer/97459) | Read how to connect Analytics to Google Sites | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Sites Help: How to use Google Sites](https://support.google.com/sites/answer/6372878) | Read how to create and publish a Google Site | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Analytics Help: URL builders (collect campaign data with UTM links)](https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/10917952) | Read the UTM rules and the example | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Google Analytics demos and tools: Campaign URL Builder](https://ga-dev-tools.web.app/ga4/campaign-url-builder/) | Open the Campaign URL Builder | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Analytics Help: Traffic acquisition report](https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/12923437) | Read how to find and read the Traffic acquisition report | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Analytics Help: Analytics Academy on Skillshop (free courses)](https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/15440208) | Optional: note the free Analytics Academy courses for later | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |

## Action task

1. Study the resources (about 45 minutes).
2. Create a one-page Google Site (or use a page you already have) and publish it.
3. Create a GA4 property and web data stream, and add the Measurement ID to the site. Check Realtime from your phone.
4. Write your UTM naming rules (lowercase, underscores) and make 3 UTM links with the Campaign URL Builder: Instagram bio, WhatsApp Status or Channel, and a YouTube description.
5. Use them for at least 7 days, then read the Traffic acquisition report and note sessions by source and campaign.

**Proof to record:** Your published site link, a screenshot of GA4 Realtime or Traffic acquisition showing your UTM sources, and your UTM tracker sheet.

**Full-time track:** Leave the UTM links running while you continue; read the report after 7 real days.

## Template: UTM naming rules and tracker

```
RULES: lowercase only; underscores, no spaces;
       source = the platform; medium = social / paid_social /
       email / qr; campaign = what or when (bio_link,
       onam_2026, pilot_week1); no personal data
Link name,Destination URL,utm_source,utm_medium,utm_campaign,utm_content,Full UTM link,Where used,Date added
```

## Template: GA4 setup checklist

```
[ ] Account created (analytics.google.com)
[ ] Property: name, India time zone, INR
[ ] Web data stream with the site URL
[ ] Enhanced measurement on
[ ] Measurement ID (G-...) added to the site
[ ] Realtime shows my own visit
[ ] 3 UTM links in use, recorded in the tracker
[ ] After 7 days: Reports > Acquisition > Traffic acquisition
```

## Common mistakes

- **Mixed capitals in UTMs.** "Instagram" and "instagram" become two sources. Use lowercase always.
- **Missing source, medium or campaign.** You'll see "(not set)". Always use all three.
- **Expecting GA4 to track WhatsApp chats.** It can't; use keywords, labels and asking customers.
- **Personal data in links.** Never put names or phone numbers in UTMs.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. Which three UTM parameters should you always use?
    - A) None
    - B) utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign
    - C) utm_name, utm_phone, utm_city
    - D) utm_term, utm_id, utm_content
2. Why must UTM values be lowercase every time?
    - A) Capitals are illegal
    - B) It hides them
    - C) They are case-sensitive, so different capitals split your data
    - D) GA4 deletes capitals
3. Where do you see which platform sent visitors in GA4?
    - A) YouTube Studio
    - B) Admin → Property settings
    - C) Reports → Acquisition → Traffic acquisition
    - D) Realtime only
4. How should you measure enquiries from a WhatsApp click-to-chat link?
    - A) You can't measure them at all
    - B) With UTMs inside the chat
    - C) GA4 tracks them automatically
    - D) With CTA keywords, WhatsApp labels and asking customers

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** Google's GA4 setup, Sites, UTM and Traffic acquisition guides (about 45 minutes)
- **Action:** set up GA4 on a simple Google Site, run 3 UTM links for 7 days and read the results. It is done when your proof is saved: your published site link, a screenshot of GA4 Realtime or Traffic acquisition showing your UTM sources, and your UTM tracker sheet.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **B.** Google says to always use these three.
2. **C.** utm_source=google and utm_source=Google are different values.
3. **C.** The report shows session source / medium and campaign.
4. **D.** The link opens a chat, not a website, so GA4 can't see it.

sections.title: SMM-M08-L03: A/B tests and client reports
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Run fair A/B tests with the tools platforms provide, judge results honestly, and write a monthly report that a busy shop owner can understand in two minutes. **Time:** about 3 hours (40 minutes study, 2 hours 20 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### Testing on social media is noisy

Every post is different: the topic, the day, the weather, what else was trending. So a "test" between two different posts is never perfectly fair. You can still learn a lot if you:

1. **Write a hypothesis first:** "A question hook will get more 3-second views than a result-first hook on food Reels."
2. **Change one thing** and keep everything else as similar as you can.
3. **Repeat it:** at least 3–4 posts per version, or use a tool that splits the audience for you.
4. **Choose the metric before you start:** the one that matches the hypothesis.
5. **Decide:** keep, drop or test again, and write it in the Experiments tab.

### Tools that split the audience for you (as of October 2026)

- **YouTube Test & compare:** test up to three titles, three thumbnails or combinations on a long video. YouTube shows the versions to different viewers and picks the winner by **watch time**, not clicks, usually within two weeks. It works in YouTube Studio on a computer only, not for Shorts, and needs advanced features turned on. Your old laptop is enough.
- **Instagram trial reels:** show a reel to non-followers first and see how it does after about 24 hours, before deciding whether to share it with followers. Useful for testing a risky idea.
- **Meta Ads A/B tests:** in Ads Manager (Module 9), with a budget.

### How sure can you be?

With small accounts, most results are **directional**. Say "this seemed to work, we'll test it again" rather than "this works". If a difference repeats in two or three tests, act on it.

### The monthly client report

Owners are busy. A good report fits on **one page**, with details after it:

1. **Goal and KPI:** "Goal: more weekday orders. KPI: WhatsApp chats from Instagram. Target: 30 a month."
2. **Headline numbers:** this month against last month and the target, with arrows and plain words.
3. **What worked:** the top 3 posts with one-line reasons.
4. **What didn't,** honestly, and why you think so.
5. **What we tested and learned.**
6. **Next month's plan:** 3 actions.
7. **What I need from you:** photos, offers, approvals.

Write in plain language (Malayalam for owners who prefer it), show screenshots, and never claim results you can't connect to your work. A short **weekly WhatsApp update** ("This week: 4 posts, 2,300 views, 11 chats; best post was ...") keeps clients confident between reports.

## Local example

Anu wrote a practice report for her own page after the challenge (made-up numbers):

> **@kuttiady.diaries, report for 1–30 November**
> **Goal:** become the page local people share. **KPIs:** views per post, shares per 1,000 views, local followers.
> **Headline:** 30 posts (target 30) ✅. Average 7-day views 1,150 (October: 310) ⬆. Shares per 1,000 views 13 (October: 6) ⬆. Followers 1,640 (start 820) ⬆.
> **What worked:** shop stories (19 shares per 1,000), collabs (most follows per view), question hooks (small lead, re-testing).
> **What didn't:** text-heavy updates (3 shares per 1,000) → moving to the WhatsApp Channel.
> **Tested:** posting at 1 pm vs 7:30 pm: similar views, faster replies at 7:30 pm.
> **December plan:** 2 shop stories a week; 1 collab; test 15 vs 30 seconds again.
> **Needs:** permission from 4 more shops for stories.

She also ran a Test & compare on her first long video's thumbnail from the laptop: the version with a face won on watch time.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [YouTube Help: A/B test titles and thumbnails](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/16391400) | Read how Test & compare works, its limits and how the winner is chosen | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [TechCrunch: Instagram trial reels (December 2024)](https://techcrunch.com/2024/12/10/instagram-rolls-out-trial-reels-that-arent-shown-to-a-creators-followers) | Re-read how trial reels work | 3 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Instagram for Creators: Finding success on reels in 2025](https://creators.instagram.com/blog/the-latest-with-instagram) | Re-read the trial reels tip | 3 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Digital Culture Network: boosted posts vs ad campaigns](https://digitalculturenetwork.org.uk/knowledge/whats-the-difference-between-boosted-posts-and-ad-campaigns-on-facebook-and-instagram/) | Read the part on A/B testing in Ads Manager (you'll use it in Module 9) | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [HubSpot Academy: Social Media Certification Course (free)](https://academy.hubspot.com/courses/social-media) | Watch the lesson on reporting and ROI (lesson names may change) | 15 min | verified 2026-10-25 |

## Action task

1. Study the resources (about 35 minutes).
2. Plan one A/B test with the template: a YouTube Test & compare on a long video (on the laptop), a trial reel test, or a two-version test across 3–4 posts each.
3. Run it, and record the result honestly as strong or directional in the Experiments tab.
4. Write a one-page monthly report for your own account using the template, with screenshots.
5. Write a weekly WhatsApp update for a pretend client in Malayalam or English.

**Proof to record:** Your A/B test plan and result, your one-page monthly report and your weekly WhatsApp update.

## Template: A/B test plan

```
HYPOTHESIS: If I ________, then ________ will rise,
            because ________.
ONE CHANGE: version A ________ / version B ________
KEPT THE SAME: topic type, length, time, day, pillar
TOOL: Test & compare / trial reel / 3-4 posts each
METRIC (chosen before): ________
RESULT: A ____ B ____  Confidence: strong / directional
DECISION: keep / drop / test again on ____
```

## Template: monthly report (one page)

```
[BUSINESS or ACCOUNT] - SOCIAL MEDIA REPORT, [MONTH]
GOAL: ______________  KPI: ____________  TARGET: ____
HEADLINE NUMBERS     This month  Last month  Target
  [KPI]              ____        ____        ____
  Posts              ____        ____        ____
  Views/reach        ____        ____
  Enquiries (chats)  ____        ____
WHAT WORKED (top 3 posts): 1. ____ 2. ____ 3. ____
WHAT DIDN'T, AND WHY: ____________________________
WHAT WE TESTED: __________ RESULT: _____________
NEXT MONTH (3 actions): 1. ____ 2. ____ 3. ____
WHAT I NEED FROM YOU: ____________________________
(Screenshots and full numbers on the next pages)
```

## Template: weekly WhatsApp update

```
EN: Hi [name], this week on Instagram: [n] posts,
[n] views, [n] WhatsApp chats. Best post: [link]
([reason]). Next week: [plan]. Can you send [photos/offer]
by [day]?
ML: നമസ്കാരം [പേര്], ഈ ആഴ്ച: [n] പോസ്റ്റുകൾ, [n] വ്യൂസ്,
[n] വാട്സാപ്പ് ചാറ്റുകൾ. മികച്ച പോസ്റ്റ്: [link].
അടുത്ത ആഴ്ച: [പ്ലാൻ]. [ഫോട്ടോ/ഓഫർ] [ദിവസം] മുൻപ് അയക്കാമോ?
```

## Common mistakes

- **Calling one comparison "proof".** Say directional, and re-test.
- **Changing the metric after seeing the results.** Choose it before the test.
- **Ten-page reports nobody reads.** One page first; details after.
- **Taking credit for everything.** Say what you can connect to your work and what you can't.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. How does YouTube's Test & compare decide the winning thumbnail?
    - A) Your choice
    - B) Most likes
    - C) Most clicks
    - D) Highest watch time
2. Which is a well-written hypothesis?
    - A) "Make it viral"
    - B) "Let's see what happens"
    - C) "Post more"
    - D) "If I use a question hook on food Reels, 3-second views will rise, because it creates curiosity"
3. What should come first in a monthly client report?
    - A) Every post's screenshot
    - B) Your hourly rate
    - C) The goal, KPI and headline numbers against last month and the target
    - D) Hashtags used
4. Where can you run YouTube Test & compare?
    - A) On Shorts only
    - B) On the phone app
    - C) In YouTube Studio on a computer, for long videos
    - D) In Instagram

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** YouTube's Test & compare, Instagram trial reels, A/B testing in ads and HubSpot's reporting lesson (about 35 minutes)
- **Action:** run one A/B test, write a one-page monthly report and a weekly WhatsApp update. It is done when your proof is saved: your A/B test plan and result, your one-page monthly report and your weekly WhatsApp update.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **D.** YouTube optimises these tests for watch time.
2. **D.** It names one change, one metric and a reason.
3. **C.** Owners need the result in two minutes; details can follow.
4. **C.** It is computer-only and not available for Shorts.

sections.title: Final self-assessment and toolkit checklist
sections.summary: Retake the baseline self-assessment, compare your account's numbers with week 0, and check that every part of your toolkit exists.
sections.content:
Two things to finish the course: retake the baseline self-assessment, and check that your toolkit is complete.

## 1. Retake the self-assessment

Open the **Baseline** tab in your SMM Workbook and fill in the **End** column for all 20 skills, without looking at your start scores first. Then compare:

- Which three skills grew the most? Put them on your portfolio's About section.
- Any skill still at 1 or 2? Note which module covers it and plan one practice task in the next month.
- Write your account's numbers now next to the week 0 numbers: followers, average views of the last 9 posts, reach and profile visits in the last 30 days, and enquiries.

## 2. Check your toolkit

Each item should be a file or link in your SMM Toolkit folder that you could show a client or an employer tomorrow. If something is missing, the module listed has its template.

| Toolkit item | Where the template is |
| --- | --- |
| SMM Workbook with every tab filled in: Posting Log, Weekly Stats, Experiments and the rest | Week 0, used all course |
| One-page social media strategy, updated with what you learned | Module 2 |
| Optimised profiles on your main and support platforms | Module 3 |
| Production kit: script formats, shot list, editing checklist, design templates | Module 4 |
| Caption bank and copy formulas, in Malayalam and English | Module 5 |
| Content system: calendar, batching routine, repurposing map, scheduling | Module 6 |
| Growth playbook: keyword and hashtag sets, collab list, engagement routine | Module 7 |
| Report templates: weekly stats, monthly client report, UTM sheet | Module 8 |
| Ad plan template and your test results (or dry-run plan) | Module 9 |
| Influencer brief, creator rate card and money plan | Module 10 |
| Three local business audits, the pilot agreement and the pilot report | Module 11 |
| Portfolio site with three case studies and before/after numbers | Modules 12 and 17 |
| AI playbook: prompts, checks and disclosure rules | Module 13 |
| Compliance and safety kit: disclosure checklist, consent form, crisis playbook, security audit | Module 14 |
| Sales kit: packages, price sheet, proposal, agreement, onboarding checklist | Module 15 |
| Wellbeing plan with your posting limits and rest days | Module 16 |

## Before you call the course done

- Save a backup of your progress from **Backup and courses** in this app, and keep it in your SMM Toolkit folder.
- Download a copy of your SMM Workbook (File → Download) so you have it offline.
- Put your next Sunday review in your calendar. The course ends; posting and learning from your numbers don't.

sections.title: What next: your 12-month roadmap
sections.summary: How to keep going after the course: first paying clients, then a niche and certifications, then an agency, a job or your own channel.
sections.content:
Finishing the course is the start of the real work. Here is a sensible order for the next twelve months.

## The next 90 days: first paying clients

- Keep posting on your own account at a rhythm you can hold, and keep the Sunday review.
- Turn your pilot business into a paying client, or use the case study to win the next one. Aim for two or three small monthly retainers (Module 15).
- Ask every client for a testimonial and a referral when results are good, with their permission to share.

## Months 4–6: get solid

- Choose a niche you enjoy and can win in, such as restaurants and bakeries, clinics and gyms, or homestays, and build templates for it.
- Do the free certifications that clients and employers recognise: [HubSpot Social Media](https://academy.hubspot.com/courses/social-media) and the [Google Ads](https://skillshop.withgoogle.com/googleads/) certifications on Skillshop.
- Raise your prices once you have three case studies with real numbers.

## Months 7–12: choose your path

| If you enjoy | Consider |
| --- | --- |
| Working with many local businesses | A small agency: one niche, two or three packages, a part-time helper (Module 15, ENT-M12-L03) |
| One brand, steady pay and a team | Jobs such as social media executive or content creator; your portfolio is your CV |
| Making content yourself | Growing your own channel towards YouTube Partner Program thresholds, affiliate income and brand deals (Module 10) |
| Ads and numbers | Paid media specialist: go deeper into Meta and Google Ads with the free official courses |

## Keep learning, free

- [Meta Blueprint free courses](https://www.facebookblueprint.com/student/page/512235-browse-free-courses-from-the-blueprint-catalog): ads, audiences and measurement
- [Google Skillshop: Free Google Ads training](https://skillshop.withgoogle.com/googleads/): Search, Display, Video and Measurement paths
- [Analytics Academy](https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/15440208): Google Analytics courses and certification
- [YouTube Creators (free official guides)](https://www.youtube.com/creators/): the Grow and Earn sections
- [OpenStax: Principles of Marketing (free textbook, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)](https://openstax.org/books/principles-marketing/pages/preface): chapters 5, 13 and 16 in full
- The **Practical Entrepreneurship** course in this app, if you want to build your own business or agency properly

## Keep up with platform changes

Platform rules change every few months. Once a month, spend 20 minutes on the official sources: [Instagram's creator best practices](https://creators.instagram.com/best-practices), [YouTube Creators](https://www.youtube.com/creators/) and the policy pages in this course's sources log. When something changes, update your templates and tell your clients.

Every link on this page was checked on 2026-10-25; see the **Sources and verification log** for each one's status.

sections.title: Glossary with Malayalam meanings
sections.summary: 101 key social media marketing terms in English and Malayalam, with simple meanings.
sections.content:
Key words from the course, roughly in the order you meet them. Many English words, such as Reel, hashtag and brand, are used as they are in Malayalam conversation; the Malayalam is given so you can explain them to shop owners and family.

| English | മലയാളം (Malayalam) | Simple meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Social media marketing** | സോഷ്യൽ മീഡിയ വിപണനം | Using social platforms to reach, engage and win customers |
| **Algorithm** | അൽഗോരിതം (നിർദ്ദേശക്രമം) | The rules and models a platform uses to decide what to show |
| **Recommendation system** | ശുപാർശ സംവിധാനം | The part of an app that picks posts for people who don't follow you |
| **Feed** | ഫീഡ് | The stream of posts you scroll through |
| **Signal** | സൂചന | A piece of information the system uses, such as watch time or shares |
| **Reach** | എത്തിച്ചേരൽ | The number of different accounts that saw your post |
| **Views** | കാഴ്ചകൾ | How many times your post was seen, counting repeats |
| **Impression** | ഇംപ്രഷൻ (പ്രദർശനം) | One time your post or thumbnail was shown |
| **Engagement** | ഇടപെടൽ | Likes, comments, shares, saves and other actions on a post |
| **Engagement rate** | ഇടപെടൽ നിരക്ക് | Interactions divided by reach (or views), as a percentage |
| **Watch time** | കണ്ട സമയം | The total time people spent watching your video |
| **Retention** | പിടിച്ചുനിർത്തൽ | How much of your video people keep watching |
| **Hook** | ആകർഷണ തുടക്കം | The first line or 1–3 seconds that make people stop and watch |
| **Call to action (CTA)** | പ്രവർത്തനാഹ്വാനം | The clear next step you ask people to take |
| **Caption** | അടിക്കുറിപ്പ് | The text that goes with a post |
| **Subtitles** | ഉപശീർഷകങ്ങൾ (സബ്‌ടൈറ്റിൽ) | On-screen text of what is said in a video |
| **Thumbnail** | ലഘുചിത്രം (തംബ്‌നെയിൽ) | The small image people see before they click a video |
| **Carousel** | കറൗസൽ (സ്ലൈഡ് പോസ്റ്റ്) | A post with several photos or slides to swipe through |
| **Reel** | റീൽ | A short vertical video on Instagram or Facebook |
| **Short** | ഷോർട്ട് | A short vertical or square video on YouTube |
| **Story** | സ്റ്റോറി | A post that disappears after 24 hours |
| **Status** | സ്റ്റാറ്റസ് | WhatsApp's 24-hour updates, seen by your contacts |
| **Broadcast** | പ്രക്ഷേപണ സന്ദേശം | One message sent privately to many contacts |
| **Channel** | ചാനൽ | A one-way feed of updates that people follow |
| **Community** | സമൂഹം (കമ്മ്യൂണിറ്റി) | A group of people who interact around shared interests |
| **Niche** | പ്രത്യേക മേഖല | The specific topic and audience an account serves |
| **Target audience** | ലക്ഷ്യ പ്രേക്ഷകർ | The people you most want to reach |
| **Persona** | ഉപഭോക്തൃ മാതൃക | A profile of a typical person in your audience, based on research |
| **Positioning** | സ്ഥാനനിർണയം | The place you want to hold in your audience's mind |
| **Competitor analysis** | എതിരാളി വിശകലനം | Studying similar accounts to learn and find gaps |
| **Content pillar** | ഉള്ളടക്ക സ്തംഭം | One of the 3–5 main themes you post about |
| **Brand voice** | ബ്രാൻഡ് ശബ്ദം | The consistent personality and tone of your writing |
| **Funnel** | ഫണൽ (വിൽപന വഴി) | The stages from first seeing you to buying and recommending |
| **Awareness** | അവബോധം | The stage where people first learn you exist |
| **Consideration** | പരിഗണന | The stage where people compare and think about buying |
| **Conversion** | പരിവർത്തനം | The moment someone takes the action you want, such as buying |
| **Loyalty** | വിശ്വസ്തത | Customers coming back again and again |
| **Objective** | ഉദ്ദേശ്യം | What social media should achieve for the business |
| **KPI (key performance indicator)** | പ്രധാന പ്രകടന സൂചകം | The main number that shows whether you are meeting a goal |
| **Vanity metric** | പൊങ്ങച്ച സംഖ്യ | A number that looks good but doesn't show business results |
| **Content calendar** | ഉള്ളടക്ക കലണ്ടർ | A plan of what to post, where and when |
| **Batching** | ഒന്നിച്ചു തയ്യാറാക്കൽ | Making several posts in one session |
| **Repurposing** | പുനരുപയോഗം | Turning one idea or video into posts for several platforms |
| **Scheduling** | സമയക്രമീകരണം | Setting a post to publish automatically later |
| **Template** | മാതൃകാരൂപം (ടെംപ്ലേറ്റ്) | A ready layout or text you reuse |
| **Keyword** | മുഖ്യപദം | A word or phrase people type when they search |
| **Hashtag** | ഹാഷ്‌ടാഗ് | A word with # that groups posts on a topic |
| **Social SEO** | സോഷ്യൽ തിരയൽ ക്രമീകരണം | Making posts easy to find in a platform's search |
| **Alt text** | ചിത്ര വിവരണം | A text description of an image for screen readers and search |
| **Trend** | പ്രവണത (ട്രെൻഡ്) | A topic, sound or format many people are using right now |
| **Collaboration (collab)** | സഹകരണം | A post or project made together with another account |
| **Direct message (DM)** | നേരിട്ടുള്ള സന്ദേശം | A private message to an account |
| **Insights (analytics)** | സ്ഥിതിവിവരക്കണക്കുകൾ | The numbers a platform gives about your posts and audience |
| **Click-through rate (CTR)** | ക്ലിക്ക് നിരക്ക് | Clicks divided by impressions, as a percentage |
| **UTM link** | യുടിഎം ലിങ്ക് (ട്രാക്കിംഗ് ലിങ്ക്) | A link with tags that tell Google Analytics where a visitor came from |
| **A/B test** | താരതമ്യ പരീക്ഷണം | Trying two versions to see which works better |
| **Hypothesis** | അനുമാനം | A guess you can test, such as "a question hook gets more views" |
| **Report** | റിപ്പോർട്ട് (വിവരണപത്രിക) | A summary of results and next steps for a client |
| **Boost** | ബൂസ്റ്റ് | Paying to show an existing post to more people |
| **Ads Manager** | ആഡ്‌സ് മാനേജർ | Meta's full tool for creating and measuring ads |
| **Campaign** | പ്രചാരണം (ക്യാമ്പെയ്ൻ) | A planned set of posts or ads with one goal and a time limit |
| **Targeting** | ലക്ഷ്യമിടൽ | Choosing who sees your ad |
| **Budget** | ബജറ്റ് (ചെലവ് പരിധി) | The most money you will spend |
| **Cost per result** | ഓരോ ഫലത്തിനുമുള്ള ചെലവ് | Ad spend divided by the number of results |
| **Retargeting** | പുനർലക്ഷ്യമിടൽ | Showing ads to people who already interacted with you |
| **Return on investment (ROI)** | നിക്ഷേപത്തിന്മേലുള്ള ആദായം | Profit gained compared with money spent |
| **ROAS** | പരസ്യച്ചെലവിന്മേലുള്ള വരുമാനം | Revenue from ads divided by ad spend |
| **Influencer** | സ്വാധീനശക്തിയുള്ളയാൾ (ഇൻഫ്ലുവൻസർ) | Someone whose content affects what their audience buys or thinks |
| **Micro-influencer** | ചെറുകിട ഇൻഫ്ലുവൻസർ | A creator with a small but close, often local, audience |
| **UGC (user-generated content)** | ഉപയോക്തൃ ഉള്ളടക്കം | Content made by customers or creators rather than the brand |
| **Affiliate marketing** | അഫിലിയേറ്റ് വിപണനം | Earning a commission when people buy through your link |
| **Monetisation** | വരുമാനമാക്കൽ | Earning money from content or an audience |
| **Disclosure** | വെളിപ്പെടുത്തൽ | Clearly saying that a post is paid, gifted or connected to a brand |
| **Material connection** | ഭൗതിക ബന്ധം | Any link with a brand, such as payment or free products, that must be disclosed |
| **Endorsement** | അംഗീകാര പ്രസ്താവന | Recommending a product as if from your own experience |
| **Copyright** | പകർപ്പവകാശം | Ownership of original creative work, such as music, photos and videos |
| **Licence** | ഉപയോഗാനുമതി (ലൈസൻസ്) | Permission to use someone's work under set conditions |
| **Consent** | സമ്മതം | Clear permission from a person before you film or post them |
| **Fake engagement** | വ്യാജ ഇടപെടൽ | Bought or automated likes, follows, views or reviews |
| **Engagement bait** | ഇടപെടൽ കെണി | Posts that beg for likes, comments or shares to trick the algorithm |
| **Dark pattern** | വഞ്ചനാപരമായ രൂപകൽപ്പന | A design trick that pushes people into choices they didn't intend |
| **Crisis** | പ്രതിസന്ധി | A problem that spreads fast and can damage a reputation |
| **Troll** | ട്രോൾ (ശല്യക്കാരൻ) | Someone who posts to provoke or hurt, not to discuss |
| **Two-step verification** | ഇരട്ട സ്ഥിരീകരണം | A second check, besides your password, when you log in |
| **Phishing** | ഫിഷിംഗ് (തട്ടിപ്പ് സന്ദേശം) | A fake message or page that tries to steal your login |
| **Google Business Profile** | ഗൂഗിൾ ബിസിനസ് പ്രൊഫൈൽ | A free listing that shows a business on Google Search and Maps |
| **Social commerce** | സോഷ്യൽ വ്യാപാരം | Selling directly through social apps and chats |
| **Catalogue** | ഉൽപ്പന്ന പട്ടിക | A list of products or services with photos and prices |
| **Review** | അഭിപ്രായം (റിവ്യൂ) | A customer's public opinion of a business |
| **Testimonial** | സാക്ഷ്യപത്രം | A customer's quote about you, shared with their permission |
| **Audit** | പരിശോധന (ഓഡിറ്റ്) | A structured check of what an account does well and badly |
| **Pilot** | പരീക്ഷണ പദ്ധതി | A short trial project to show results before a paid contract |
| **Case study** | കേസ് സ്റ്റഡി (വിജയകഥ) | A short story of a project with before and after numbers |
| **Portfolio** | പ്രവൃത്തി ശേഖരം | A collection of your best work to show clients |
| **Personal brand** | വ്യക്തിഗത ബ്രാൻഡ് | What people know and trust you for |
| **Retainer** | മാസവരി കരാർ | A monthly fee for ongoing work |
| **Proposal** | നിർദ്ദേശപത്രിക | A document that offers your service, price and plan to a client |
| **Onboarding** | തുടക്ക നടപടികൾ | The steps to start work with a new client |
| **Agency** | ഏജൻസി | A business that does marketing work for several clients |
| **Burnout** | അമിതജോലി മൂലമുള്ള തളർച്ച | Exhaustion from long-term work stress that isn't managed |
| **Synthetic content** | കൃത്രിമമായി നിർമ്മിച്ച ഉള്ളടക്കം | AI-generated or AI-altered images, video or audio that look real |

sections.title: Sources and verification log
sections.summary: Every link in the course, where it is used and when it was checked (2026-10-25).
sections.content:
Every link in this course is listed here with the date it was checked. Links were opened and read on 2026-10-25; nothing here was copied from memory. If a link stops working, search for its title on the same website.

- **verified 2026-10-25:** the page was opened and its content matched what the course says.
- **verified 2026-10-25 (page title checked):** the page only shows its text in a full browser, so its title and description were checked. The facts the course takes from it come from another linked source.
- **check current rules:** a rule, feature, limit or fee that changes often. Open the official source before you act or advise a client.
- **unverified:** the site blocks automated checks, so the page could not be opened for this course. The address is the official one named by other government sources; type it yourself and check it is the real site.

Several Meta help pages (facebook.com and parts of WhatsApp's help) block automated checks completely, so this course doesn't link to them; it uses Meta's readable official blogs, the Blueprint course pages and dated news reports instead. OpenStax *Principles of Marketing* is licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and this course only links to it.
